Widget Classes¶

Widget Base Classes¶

Widget¶

class urwid.Widget¶

Widget base class.

_selectable = False¶

The default selectable() method returns this value.

_sizing = frozenset(['flow', 'box', 'fixed'])¶

The default sizing() method returns this value.

_command_map = urwid.command_map¶

A shared CommandMap instance. May be redefined in subclasses or widget instances.

rows(size, focus=False)¶

Note

This method is not implemented in Widget but must be implemented by any flow widget. See sizing().

See Widget.render() for parameter details.

Returns:

The number of rows required for this widget given a number of columns in size

This is the method flow widgets use to communicate their size to other widgets without having to render a canvas. This should be a quick calculation as this function may be called a number of times in normal operation. If your implementation may take a long time you should add your own caching here.

There is some metaclass magic defined in the Widget metaclass WidgetMeta that causes the result of this function to be retrieved from any canvas cached by CanvasCache, so if your widget has been rendered you may not receive calls to this function. The class variable ignore_focus may be defined and set to True if this widget renders the same size regardless of the value of the focus parameter.

get_cursor_coords(size)¶

Note

This method is not implemented in Widget but must be implemented by any widget that may return cursor coordinates as part of the canvas that render() returns.

Parameters:

size – See Widget.render() for details.

Returns:

(col, row) if this widget has a cursor, None otherwise

Return the cursor coordinates (col, row) of a cursor that will appear as part of the canvas rendered by this widget when in focus, or None if no cursor is displayed.

The ListBox widget uses this method to make sure a cursor in the focus widget is not scrolled out of view. It is a separate method to avoid having to render the whole widget while calculating layout.

Container widgets will typically call the get_cursor_coords() method on their focus widget.

get_pref_col(size)¶

Note

This method is not implemented in Widget but may be implemented by a subclass.

Parameters:

size – See Widget.render() for details.

Returns:

a column number or 'left' for the leftmost available column or 'right' for the rightmost available column

Return the preferred column for the cursor to be displayed in this widget. This value might not be the same as the column returned from get_cursor_coords().

The ListBox and Pile widgets call this method on a widget losing focus and use the value returned to call move_cursor_to_coords() on the widget becoming the focus. This allows the focus to move up and down through widgets while keeping the cursor in approximately the same column on screen.

move_cursor_to_coords(size, col, row)¶

Note

This method is not implemented in Widget but may be implemented by a subclass. Not implementing this method is equivalent to having a method that always returns False.

Parameters:

  • size – See Widget.render() for details.

  • col – new column for the cursor, 0 is the left edge of this widget

  • row – new row for the cursor, 0 it the top row of this widget

Returns:

True if the position was set successfully anywhere on row, False otherwise

Initialize a logger scoped to the concrete widget subclass.

_emit(name: Hashable, *args: Any) → None¶

Emit signals with self as first argument.

_invalidate() → None¶

Mark cached canvases rendered by this widget as dirty so that they will not be used again.

Read-only property that steps through decoration widgets and returns the one at the base.

This default implementation returns self.

property focus: AbstractWidget | None¶

Read-only property returning the child widget in focus for container widgets.

This default implementation always returns None, indicating that this widget has no children.

property focus_position: Any¶

Read or set the focus position for container widgets.

This default implementation raises IndexError, making normal widgets fail the same way accessing focus_position on an empty container widget would.

Raises:

IndexError – this widget is not a container widget.

Keyboard input handler.

Parameters:

Returns:

None if key was handled, key (the same value passed) if it was not handled

Warns WidgetWarning:

mouse_event(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], event: str, button: int, col: int, row: int, focus: bool) → bool | None¶

Mouse event handler.

Parameters:

  • size – See Widget.render() for details.

  • event – Values such as 'mouse press', 'ctrl mouse press', 'mouse release', 'meta mouse release', 'mouse drag'; see Mouse Input

  • button – 1 through 5 for press events, often 0 for release events (which button was released is often not known)

  • col – Column of the event, 0 is the left edge of this widget

  • row – Row of the event, 0 it the top row of this widget

  • focus – Set to True if this widget or one of its children is in focus

Returns:

True if the event was handled by this widget, False otherwise

Warns WidgetWarning:

the widget is not selectable and its class did not call super().__init__().

pack(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → tuple[int, int]¶

See Widget.render() for parameter details.

Returns:

A “packed” size (maxcol, maxrow) for this widget

Raises:

  • NotImplementedError – the widget supports FIXED sizing but does not override this method.

  • WidgetError – size does not match any sizing mode the widget supports.

Calculate and return a minimum size where all content could still be displayed. Fixed widgets must implement this method and return their size when () is passed as the size parameter.

This default implementation returns the size passed, or the maxcol passed and the value of rows() as the maxrow when (maxcol,) is passed as the size parameter.

Note

This is a new method that hasn’t been fully implemented across the standard widget types. In particular it has not yet been implemented for container widgets.

Text widgets have implemented this method. You can use Text.pack() to calculate the minimum columns and rows required to display a text widget without wrapping, or call it iteratively to calculate the minimum number of columns required to display the text wrapped into a target number of rows.

render(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → Canvas¶

Render widget and produce canvas.

Parameters:

  • size –

    One of the following, maxcol and maxrow are integers > 0:

    (maxcol, maxrow)

    for box sizing – the parent chooses the exact size of this widget

    (maxcol,)

    for flow sizing – the parent chooses only the number of columns for this widget

    ()

    for fixed sizing – this widget is a fixed size which can’t be adjusted by the parent

  • focus – set to True if this widget or one of its children is in focus

Returns:

A Canvas subclass instance containing the rendered content of this widget

Raises:

NotImplementedError – the subclass does not implement rendering.

Text widgets return a TextCanvas (arbitrary text and display attributes), SolidFill widgets return a SolidCanvas (a single character repeated across the whole surface) and container widgets return a CompositeCanvas (one or more other canvases arranged arbitrarily).

If focus is False, the returned canvas may not have a cursor position set.

There is some metaclass magic defined in the Widget metaclass WidgetMeta that causes the result of this method to be cached by CanvasCache. Later calls will automatically look up the value in the cache first.

As a small optimization the class variable ignore_focus may be defined and set to True if this widget renders the same canvas regardless of the value of the focus parameter.

Any time the content of a widget changes it should call _invalidate() to remove any cached canvases, or the widget may render the cached canvas instead of creating a new one.

selectable() → bool¶

Return whether this widget is designed to take the focus.

Returns:

True if this widget contains something the user might want to interact with, False otherwise.

This default implementation returns _selectable. Subclasses may leave it as is if they are not selectable, or, if they are always selectable, set the _selectable class variable to True.

If this method returns True then the Widget.keypress() method must be implemented.

Returning False does not guarantee that this widget will never be in focus, only that this widget will usually be skipped over when changing focus. It is still possible for non selectable widgets to have the focus (typically when there are no other selectable widgets visible).

sizing() → frozenset[Sizing]¶

Return the sizing modes this widget supports.

Returns:

A frozenset including one or more of 'box', 'flow' and 'fixed'. Default implementation returns the value of _sizing, which for this class includes all three.

The sizing modes returned indicate the modes that may be supported by this widget, but is not sufficient to know that using that sizing mode will work. Subclasses should make an effort to remove sizing modes they know will not work given the state of the widget, but many do not yet do this.

If a sizing mode is missing from the set then the widget should fail when used in that mode.

If 'flow' is among the values returned then the other methods in this widget must be able to accept a single-element tuple (maxcol,) to their size parameter, and the rows() method must be defined.

If 'box' is among the values returned then the other methods must be able to accept a two-element tuple (maxcol, maxrow) to their size parameter.

If 'fixed' is among the values returned then the other methods must be able to accept an empty tuple () to their size parameter, and the pack() method must be defined.

WidgetWrap¶

class urwid.WidgetWrap(w: WrappedWidget)¶

Base class for widgets that compose another widget for their display and behaviour.

Parameters:

w – widget to wrap, stored as self._w

This object will pass the functions defined in Widget interface definition to self._w.

The purpose of this widget is to provide a base class for widgets that compose other widgets for their display and behaviour. The details of that composition should not affect users of the subclass. The subclass may decide to expose some of the wrapped widgets by behaving like a ContainerWidget or WidgetDecoration, or it may hide them from outside access.

Deprecated since version 2.4.0: Wrapping an object that does not implement the Widget API (see AbstractWidget) is deprecated. Support will be removed in version 7.0.

enter_selectable(*, reverse: bool = False) → None¶

Forward the entry hook to the wrapped widget, when it has one.

A container with select_navigation calls this when it moves its focus to this widget, see Moving the Focus with Tab. The hook goes to the widget that keypress() sends keys to: a subclass that sends keys elsewhere overrides this method to match.

Parameters:

reverse – start at the last selectable widget instead of the first one.

WidgetDecoration¶

class urwid.WidgetDecoration(original_widget: WrappedWidget)¶

Base class for decoration widgets: widgets that contain one or more widgets and only ever have a single focus.

This type of widget will affect the display or behaviour of the original_widget, but it is not part of determining a chain of focus.

Parameters:

original_widget – the widget being decorated

Don’t actually do this - use a WidgetDecoration subclass instead, these are not real widgets:

>>> from urwid import Text
>>> WidgetDecoration(Text("hi"))
<WidgetDecoration fixed/flow widget <Text fixed/flow widget 'hi'>>

Warning

WidgetDecoration does not implement the render method. Implement it, or forward to the wrapped widget, in the subclass.

Wrap original_widget, warning when it does not implement the Widget API.

Deprecated since version 2.4.0: Wrapping an object that does not implement the Widget API (see AbstractWidget) is deprecated. Support will be removed in version 7.0.

property base_widget: AbstractWidget¶

Return the widget without decorations.

If there is only one Decoration, then this is the same as original_widget. The walk stops at a unittest.mock object.

>>> from urwid import Text
>>> t = Text("hello")
>>> wd1 = WidgetDecoration(t)
>>> wd2 = WidgetDecoration(wd1)
>>> wd3 = WidgetDecoration(wd2)
>>> wd3.original_widget is wd2
True
>>> wd3.base_widget is t
True
enter_selectable(*, reverse: bool = False) → None¶

Forward the entry hook to original_widget, when it has one.

A container with select_navigation calls this when it moves its focus to this widget, see Moving the Focus with Tab. The hook goes to the widget that keypress() sends keys to: a subclass that sends keys elsewhere overrides this method to match.

Parameters:

reverse – start at the last selectable widget instead of the first one.

property original_widget: WrappedWidget¶

Return the widget this decoration wraps.

selectable() → bool¶

Return whether the wrapped widget can take the input focus.

sizing() → frozenset[Sizing]¶

Return the set of sizing modes supported by the wrapped widget.

WidgetContainerMixin¶

class urwid.WidgetContainerMixin(*args, **kwargs)¶

Mixin class for widget containers implementing common container methods.

abstract property focus: AbstractWidget | None¶

Read-only property returning the child widget in focus for container widgets.

This default implementation always returns None, indicating that this widget has no children.

get_focus_path() → list[int | str]¶

Return the .focus_position values starting from this container.

Proceeds along each child widget until reaching a leaf (non-container) widget.

get_focus_widgets() → list[WidgetContainerMixin[Any] | AbstractWidget]¶

Return the .focus values starting from this container.

Proceeds along each child widget until reaching a leaf (non-container) widget.

Note that the list does not contain the topmost container widget (i.e., on which this method is called), but does include the lowest leaf widget.

set_focus_path(positions: Iterable[int | str]) → None¶

Set the .focus_position property starting from this container widget.

Proceeds along newly focused child widgets. Any failed assignment due to incompatible position types or invalid positions will raise an IndexError.

This method may be used to restore a particular widget to the focus by passing in the value returned from an earlier call to get_focus_path().

Parameters:

positions – sequence of positions

SelectNavigationMixin¶

class urwid.SelectNavigationMixin(*args, **kwargs)¶

Mixin for container widgets that handle the 'next selectable' and 'prev selectable' commands.

The behaviour is described in Moving the Focus with Tab. A container class that uses it is a Widget and:

  • implements the WidgetContainerMixin interface, with a settable focus_position;

  • implements _select_candidates() and _select_enter_focus();

  • in keypress(), passes a select command that its child in focus returned unhandled to _select_keypress_unhandled() when select_navigation is set.

SelectNavigationListContentsMixin implements both methods for containers with list contents.

A container that keeps the Widget.focus_position of Widget, which raises IndexError, is a single stop instead: the select commands are returned unhandled, its focus is not changed, and a WidgetWarning names the class.

abstractmethod _select_candidates(*, reverse: bool, from_edge: bool) → Iterator[Any]¶

Yield the positions of the selectable children in the traversal order.

Positions are produced lazily, so the search stops at the first one used.

Parameters:

  • reverse – yield them from the last to the first.

  • from_edge – start at the first (last when reverse) position instead of after the focus.

abstractmethod _select_enter_focus(*, reverse: bool) → None¶

Call enter_selectable(reverse=reverse) of the child in focus, when it has one.

_select_keypress_unhandled(key: str) → str | None¶

Handle a select command that the child in focus returned unhandled.

Move the focus to the next (previous) selectable child and enter it. Past the last (first) one, focus the first (last) selectable child, enter it and return key, so an opted-in parent moves on to its own next child.

enter_selectable(*, reverse: bool = False) → None¶

Start at the first selectable child, or at the last one when reverse is set.

It is the entry hook a parent container calls, and acts only when select_navigation is set, see Moving the Focus with Tab.

Parameters:

reverse – start at the last selectable child instead of the first one.

focus_first_selectable() → bool¶

Focus the first selectable child through the focus_position setter and enter it.

It acts whether or not select_navigation is set, see Moving the Focus with Tab.

Returns:

whether a selectable child exists.

focus_last_selectable() → bool¶

Focus the last selectable child through the focus_position setter and enter it.

It acts whether or not select_navigation is set, see Moving the Focus with Tab.

Returns:

whether a selectable child exists.

select_navigation: bool = False¶

Whether the container handles the 'next selectable' and 'prev selectable' commands. The urwid containers set it from their select_navigation argument; the class default keeps a subclass that does not set it working, with the commands left unhandled.

SelectNavigationListContentsMixin¶

class urwid.SelectNavigationListContentsMixin(*args, **kwargs)¶

SelectNavigationMixin for containers whose positions are indexes into self.contents.

It implements _select_candidates() and _select_enter_focus() from contents and focus_position only, in the order of contents. A child whose options start with (GIVEN, 0) is not drawn, so it is not a candidate.

abstract property contents: MutableSequence[_ContentsItem]¶

Return the contents of container as a list of (widget, options).

abstract property focus_position: int¶

Index of child widget in focus.

Basic Widget Classes¶

Text¶

class urwid.Text(markup: _TagMarkup, align: Literal['left', 'center', 'right'] | Align = Align.LEFT, wrap: Literal['space', 'any', 'clip', 'ellipsis'] | WrapMode = WrapMode.SPACE, layout: text_layout.TextLayout | None = None, *, selectable: bool = False)¶

A horizontally resizeable text widget.

Parameters:

  • markup –

    content of text widget, one of:

    bytes or unicode

    text to be displayed

    (display attribute, text markup)

    text markup with display attribute applied to all parts of text markup with no display attribute already applied

    [text markup, text markup, … ]

    all text markup in the list joined together

  • align – typically 'left', 'center' or 'right'

  • wrap – typically 'space', 'any', 'clip' or 'ellipsis'

  • layout – defaults to a shared StandardTextLayout instance

  • selectable – True makes the widget take the focus, for example as a row of a list that is chosen by moving the focus to it; it shows no cursor and returns every key

>>> Text("Hello")
<Text fixed/flow widget 'Hello'>
>>> t = Text(("bold", "stuff"), "right", "any")
>>> t
<Text fixed/flow widget 'stuff' align='right' wrap='any'>
>>> print(t.text)
stuff
>>> t.attrib
[('bold', 5)]
>>> Text("Row", selectable=True)
<Text selectable fixed/flow widget 'Row'>
property attrib: list[tuple[Hashable, int]]¶

Read-only property returning the run-length encoded display attributes of this widget.

get_line_translation(maxcol: int, ta: tuple[str | bytes, list[tuple[Hashable, int]]] | None = None) → list[list[tuple[int, int, int | bytes] | tuple[int, int | None]]]¶

Return layout structure used to map self.text to a canvas.

This method is used internally, but may be useful for debugging custom layout classes.

Parameters:

  • maxcol – columns available for display

  • ta – None or the (text, display attributes) tuple returned from get_text()

get_text() → tuple[str | bytes, list[tuple[Hashable, int]]]¶

Return (text, display attributes).

text

complete bytes/unicode content of text widget

display attributes

run length encoded display attributes for text, eg. [('attr1', 10), ('attr2', 5)]; nested markup gives a LayeredAttr of the inner and the enclosing attributes

>>> Text("Hello").get_text()
('Hello', [])
>>> Text(("bright", "Headline")).get_text()
('Headline', [('bright', 8)])
>>> Text([("a", "one"), "two", ("b", "three")]).get_text()
('onetwothree', [('a', 3), (None, 3), ('b', 5)])
>>> Text(("a", ["one", ("b", "two")])).get_text()
('onetwo', [('a', 3), (LayeredAttr('b', 'a'), 3)])
property layout: TextLayout¶

Return the TextLayout instance used to lay out and wrap this widget’s text.

pack(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | None = None, focus: bool = False) → tuple[int, int]¶

Return the number of screen columns and rows required for this Text widget.

The widget is expected to be displayed without wrapping or clipping, as a single element tuple. With maxcol the size is taken from the layout at that width. Without it the width is searched for:

maxcol = text width + 1, with StandardTextLayout tabs at their widest
    |
    v
lay out at maxcol --> layout has pack()? --no--> widest line, line count
    ^                        |
    |                       yes
    |                        v
double maxcol <--no-- layout.pack() < maxcol? --yes--> pack() columns, line count
Parameters:

  • size – None or () for unlimited screen columns (like FIXED sizing) or (maxcol,) to specify a maximum column size

  • focus – widget is focused on

>>> Text("important things").pack()
(16, 1)
>>> Text("important things").pack((15,))
(9, 2)
>>> Text("important things").pack((8,))
(8, 2)
>>> Text("important things").pack(())
(16, 1)
>>> not_common_separated_text = (
...     "Line feed" + chr(10) + "Line Separator" + chr(0x2028) + "Paragraph Separator" + chr(0x2029)
... )
>>> # U+2028 (Line Separator) and U+2029 (Paragraph Separator) are not splitted by StandardTextLayout
>>> not_common_separated = Text(not_common_separated_text)

>>> not_common_separated.pack()
(33, 2)
>>> not_common_separated_canv = not_common_separated.render(())
>>> not_common_separated_canv.cols()
33
>>> not_common_separated_canv.rows()
2
render(size: tuple[int] | tuple[()], focus: bool = False) → TextCanvas¶

Render contents with wrapping and alignment. Return canvas.

See Widget.render() for parameter details.

>>> Text("important things").render((18,)).text
[b'important things  ']
>>> Text("important things").render((11,)).text
[b'important  ', b'things     ']
>>> Text("demo text").render(()).text
[b'demo text']
rows(size: tuple[int], focus: bool = False) → int¶

Return the number of rows the rendered text requires.

See Widget.rows() for parameter details.

>>> Text("important things").rows((18,))
1
>>> Text("important things").rows((11,))
2
set_align_mode(mode: Literal['left', 'center', 'right'] | Align) → None¶

Set text alignment mode.

Supported modes depend on text layout object in use but defaults to a StandardTextLayout instance.

Parameters:

mode – typically 'left', 'center' or 'right'

Raises:

TextError – mode is not supported by the layout in use.

>>> t = Text("word")
>>> t.set_align_mode("right")
>>> t.align
'right'
>>> t.render((10,)).text  # ... = b in Python 3
[...'      word']
>>> t.align = "center"
>>> t.render((10,)).text
[...'   word   ']
>>> t.align = "somewhere"
Traceback (most recent call last):
TextError: Alignment mode 'somewhere' not supported.
set_layout(align: Literal['left', 'center', 'right'] | Align, wrap: Literal['space', 'any', 'clip', 'ellipsis'] | WrapMode, layout: text_layout.TextLayout | None = None) → None¶

Set the text layout object, alignment and wrapping modes at the same time.

Parameters:

  • align – typically ‘left’, ‘center’ or ‘right’

  • wrap – typically ‘space’, ‘any’, ‘clip’ or ‘ellipsis’

  • layout – defaults to a shared StandardTextLayout instance

>>> t = Text("hi")
>>> t.set_layout("right", "clip")
>>> t
<Text fixed/flow widget 'hi' align='right' wrap='clip'>
set_text(markup: _TagMarkup) → None¶

Set content of text widget.

Parameters:

markup – see Text for description.

>>> t = Text("foo")
>>> print(t.text)
foo
>>> t.set_text("bar")
>>> print(t.text)
bar
>>> t.text = "baz"  # not supported because text stores text but set_text() takes markup
Traceback (most recent call last):
AttributeError: can't set attribute
set_wrap_mode(mode: Literal['space', 'any', 'clip', 'ellipsis'] | WrapMode) → None¶

Set text wrapping mode.

Supported modes depend on text layout object in use but defaults to a StandardTextLayout instance.

Parameters:

mode – typically 'space', 'any', 'clip' or 'ellipsis'

Raises:

TextError – mode is not supported by the layout in use.

>>> t = Text("some words")
>>> t.render((6,)).text  # ... = b in Python 3
[...'some  ', ...'words ']
>>> t.set_wrap_mode("clip")
>>> t.wrap
'clip'
>>> t.render((6,)).text
[...'some w']
>>> t.wrap = "any"  # Urwid 0.9.9 or later
>>> t.render((6,)).text
[...'some w', ...'ords  ']
>>> t.wrap = "somehow"
Traceback (most recent call last):
TextError: Wrap mode 'somehow' not supported.
property text: str | bytes¶

Read-only property returning the complete bytes/unicode content of this widget.

Edit¶

class urwid.Edit(caption: _TagMarkup = '', edit_text: str = '', multiline: bool = False, align: Literal['left', 'center', 'right'] | Align = Align.LEFT, wrap: Literal['space', 'any', 'clip', 'ellipsis'] | WrapMode = WrapMode.SPACE, allow_tab: bool = False, edit_pos: int | None = None, layout: text_layout.TextLayout | None = None, mask: str | None = None, *, expand_tabs: bool = True, max_length: int | None = None)¶

Text editing widget implements cursor movement, text insertion and deletion.

A caption may prefix the editing area. Uses text class for text layout.

Users of this class may listen for "change" or "postchange" events. See :func:connect_signal.

  • "change" is sent just before the value of edit_text changes. It receives the new text as an argument. Note that "change" cannot change the text in question as edit_text changes the text afterwards.

  • "postchange" is sent after the value of edit_text changes. It receives the old value of the text as an argument and thus is appropriate for changing the text. It is possible for a "postchange" event handler to get into a loop of changing the text and then being called when the event is re-emitted. It is up to the event handler to guard against this case (for instance, by not changing the text if it is signaled for text that it has already changed once).

  • "submit" is sent when enter, mapped to 'activate', reaches an Edit with multiline=False. It receives the edit text as an argument. keypress() still returns the key.

Create the Edit widget.

Parameters:

  • caption – markup for caption preceding edit_text, see Text for description of text markup.

  • edit_text – initial text for editing, type (bytes or str) must match the text in the caption

  • multiline – True: enter inserts a newline, False: return it

  • align – typically ‘left’, ‘center’ or ‘right’

  • wrap – typically ‘space’, ‘any’ or ‘clip’

  • allow_tab – True: tab is inserted, False: return it

  • edit_pos – initial position for cursor, None:end of edit_text

  • layout – defaults to a shared StandardTextLayout instance

  • mask – hide text entered with this character, None:disable mask

  • expand_tabs – True: an inserted tab is spaces up to the next tab stop of the line, False: a tab character

  • max_length – the longest edit_text allowed, see max_length

Raises:

ValueError – max_length is negative, or edit_text is longer than it.

>>> Edit()
<Edit selectable flow widget '' edit_pos=0>
>>> Edit("Y/n? ", "yes")
<Edit selectable flow widget 'yes' caption='Y/n? ' edit_pos=3>
>>> Edit("Name ", "Smith", edit_pos=1)
<Edit selectable flow widget 'Smith' caption='Name ' edit_pos=1>
>>> Edit("", "3.14", align="right")
<Edit selectable flow widget '3.14' align='right' edit_pos=4>
>>> pin = Edit("PIN: ", "123", max_length=4)
>>> pin.keypress((20,), "4")
>>> pin.keypress((20,), "5")
'5'
>>> print(pin.edit_text)
1234
property attrib: list[tuple[Hashable, int]]¶

Read-only property returning the run-length encoded display attributes of this widget.

property caption: str | bytes¶

Read-only property returning the caption for this widget.

property edit_pos¶

Property controlling the edit position for this widget.

property edit_text: str¶

Property controlling the edit text for this widget.

get_cursor_coords(size: tuple[int]) → tuple[int, int] | None¶

Return the (x, y) coordinates of cursor within widget, or None when it has no columns to show it in.

>>> Edit("? ", "yes").get_cursor_coords((10,))
(5, 0)
>>> Edit("? ", "yes").get_cursor_coords((0,)) is None
True
get_edit_text() → str¶

Return the edit text for this widget.

>>> e = Edit("What? ", "oh, nothing.")
>>> print(e.get_edit_text())
oh, nothing.
>>> print(e.edit_text)
oh, nothing.
get_line_translation(maxcol: int, ta: tuple[str | bytes, list[tuple[Hashable, int]]] | None = None) → list[list[tuple[int, int, int | bytes] | tuple[int, int | None]]]¶

Return the line translation for ta, shifted to keep the cursor visible if needed.

get_pref_col(size: tuple[int]) → int¶

Return the preferred column for the cursor, or the current cursor x value.

May also return 'left' or 'right' to indicate the leftmost or rightmost column available.

This method is used internally and by other widgets when moving the cursor up or down between widgets so that the column selected is one that the user would expect.

>>> size = (10,)
>>> Edit().get_pref_col(size)
0
>>> e = Edit("", "word")
>>> e.get_pref_col(size)
4
>>> e.keypress(size, "left")
>>> e.get_pref_col(size)
3
>>> e.keypress(size, "end")
>>> e.get_pref_col(size)
<Align.RIGHT: 'right'>
>>> e = Edit("", "2\nwords")
>>> e.keypress(size, "left")
>>> e.keypress(size, "up")
>>> e.get_pref_col(size)
4
>>> e.keypress(size, "left")
>>> e.get_pref_col(size)
0
get_text() → tuple[str | bytes, list[tuple[Hashable, int]]]¶

Return (text, display attributes).

See Text.get_text() for details.

Text returned includes the caption and edit_text, possibly masked.

>>> Edit("What? ", "oh, nothing.").get_text()
('What? oh, nothing.', [])
>>> Edit(("bright", "user@host:~$ "), "ls").get_text()
('user@host:~$ ls', [('bright', 13)])
>>> Edit("password:", "seekrit", mask="*").get_text()
('password:*******', [])
insert_text(text: str) → None¶

Insert text at the cursor position and update cursor.

This method is used by the keypress() method when inserting one or more characters into edit_text.

Parameters:

text – text for inserting, type (bytes or unicode) must match the text in the caption

Raises:

ValueError – the result is longer than max_length; the text is left as it was.

>>> e = Edit("", "42")
>>> e.insert_text(".5")
>>> e
<Edit selectable flow widget '42.5' edit_pos=4>
>>> e.set_edit_pos(2)
>>> e.insert_text("a")
>>> print(e.edit_text)
42a.5
insert_text_result(text: str) → tuple[str | bytes, int]¶

Return result of insert_text(text) without actually performing the insertion.

Handy for pre-validation.

Parameters:

text – text for inserting, type (bytes or unicode) must match the text in the caption

Raises:

ValueError – text cannot be inserted at the current edit position. The message carries the texts involved unless a mask is set.

keypress(size: tuple[int], key: str) → str | None¶

Handle editing keystrokes, return others.

A key whose text would make edit_text longer than max_length inserts nothing and is returned, as IntEdit returns a digit past its limit. A tab is inserted whole or not at all.

The readline delete commands described in CommandMap go through set_edit_text(). A subclass whose set_edit_text() raises for some text has to handle those commands itself once an application binds them, or the exception leaves keypress().

>>> e, size = Edit(), (20,)
>>> e.keypress(size, "x")
>>> e.keypress(size, "left")
>>> e.keypress(size, "1")
>>> print(e.edit_text)
1x
>>> e.keypress(size, "backspace")
>>> e.keypress(size, "end")
>>> e.keypress(size, "2")
>>> print(e.edit_text)
x2
>>> e.keypress(size, "shift f1")
'shift f1'
Raises:

ValueError – the preferred cursor column could not be determined.

property layout: TextLayout¶

Return the TextLayout instance used to lay out and wrap this widget’s text.

property max_length: int | None¶

The longest edit_text allowed, or None for no limit.

It is counted like edit_pos: in code points, or in bytes when the caption is bytes. A key that would go over it is refused, see keypress(); set_edit_text() and insert_text() raise ValueError instead. Setting it negative or below the length of edit_text raises ValueError too.

mouse_event(size: tuple[int], event: str, button: int, col: int, row: int, focus: bool) → bool | None¶

Move the cursor to the location clicked for button 1.

>>> size = (20,)
>>> e = Edit("", "words here")
>>> e.mouse_event(size, "mouse press", 1, 2, 0, True)
True
>>> e.edit_pos
2
move_cursor_to_coords(size: tuple[int], x: int | Literal[Align.LEFT, Align.RIGHT], y: int) → bool¶

Set the cursor position with (x,y) coordinates.

Returns:

True if move succeeded, False otherwise.

>>> size = (10,)
>>> e = Edit("", "edit\ntext")
>>> e.move_cursor_to_coords(size, 5, 0)
True
>>> e.edit_pos
4
>>> e.move_cursor_to_coords(size, 5, 3)
False
>>> e.move_cursor_to_coords(size, 0, 1)
True
>>> e.edit_pos
5
position_coords(maxcol: int, pos: int) → tuple[int, int]¶

Return (x, y) coordinates for an offset into self.edit_text.

render(size: tuple[int], focus: bool = False) → TextCanvas | CompositeCanvas¶

Render edit widget and return canvas.

Include cursor when in focus.

>>> edit = Edit("? ", "yes")
>>> c = edit.render((10,), focus=True)
>>> c.text
[b'? yes     ']
>>> c.cursor
(5, 0)
selectable() → bool¶

Return True: this widget is always selectable.

Wrapped Text widget is not selectable while the edit widget has to be selectable.

set_align_mode(mode: Literal['left', 'center', 'right'] | Align) → None¶

Set text alignment mode. See Text.set_align_mode() for details.

set_caption(caption: _TagMarkup) → None¶

Set the caption markup for this widget.

Parameters:

caption – markup for caption preceding edit_text, see Text.__init__() for description of text markup.

>>> e = Edit("")
>>> e.set_caption("cap1")
>>> print(e.caption)
cap1
>>> e.set_caption(("bold", "cap2"))
>>> print(e.caption)
cap2
>>> e.attrib
[('bold', 4)]
>>> e.caption = "cap3"  # not supported because caption stores text but set_caption() takes markup
Traceback (most recent call last):
AttributeError: can't set attribute
set_edit_pos(pos: int) → None¶

Set the cursor position with a self.edit_text offset.

Clips pos to [0, len(edit_text)].

Parameters:

pos – cursor position

>>> e = Edit("", "word")
>>> e.edit_pos
4
>>> e.set_edit_pos(2)
>>> e.edit_pos
2
>>> e.edit_pos = -1  # Urwid 0.9.9 or later
>>> e.edit_pos
0
>>> e.edit_pos = 20
>>> e.edit_pos
4
set_edit_text(text: str, *, edit_pos: int | None = None) → None¶

Set the edit text for this widget.

Parameters:

  • text – text for editing, type (bytes or unicode) must match the text in the caption

  • edit_pos – cursor position to set before "postchange" is sent, clipped as by set_edit_pos(); None keeps the current position, clipped to the new text. An override passes None on unchanged: an editing key gives its position to this method by another route, which an explicit position replaces.

Raises:

ValueError – text is longer than max_length; the text is left as it was.

>>> e = Edit()
>>> e.set_edit_text("yes")
>>> print(e.edit_text)
yes
>>> e
<Edit selectable flow widget 'yes' edit_pos=0>
>>> e.edit_text = "no"  # Urwid 0.9.9 or later
>>> print(e.edit_text)
no
>>> e.set_edit_text("maybe", edit_pos=5)
>>> e.edit_pos
5
set_layout(align: Literal['left', 'center', 'right'] | Align, wrap: Literal['space', 'any', 'clip', 'ellipsis'] | WrapMode, layout: text_layout.TextLayout | None = None) → None¶

Set the text layout object, alignment and wrapping modes at the same time.

See Text.set_layout() for details.

set_mask(mask: str | None) → None¶

Set the character for masking text away.

Parameters:

mask – hide text entered with this character, None:disable mask

set_wrap_mode(mode: Literal['space', 'any', 'clip', 'ellipsis'] | WrapMode) → None¶

Set text wrapping mode. See Text.set_wrap_mode() for details.

sizing() → frozenset[Sizing]¶

Sizing information.

Edit widget sizing is narrower than Text: we cannot predict the final input length.

property text: str | bytes¶

Read-only property returning the complete bytes/unicode content of this widget.

Includes caption plus edit_text, possibly masked.

valid_char(ch: str) → bool¶

Filter for text that may be entered into this widget by the user.

Parameters:

ch – character to be inserted

This implementation returns True for a wide character and for any single character that is not a control character (Unicode category Cc): the displays print a control character as ? while the width calculation counts it as zero columns. A single byte is accepted unless it is a C0 control or DEL, because 0x80-0xff are printable characters in a single-byte encoding.

IntEdit¶

class urwid.IntEdit(caption: _TagMarkup = '', default: int | str | None = None)¶

Edit widget for integer values.

Create the IntEdit widget.

Parameters:

  • caption – caption markup

  • default – default edit value

>>> IntEdit("", 42)
<IntEdit selectable flow widget '42' edit_pos=2>
insert_text(text: str) → None¶

Insert text at the cursor position and update the cursor, removing the leading zeros before the cursor.

The result is set at once, so “change” and “postchange” are sent once, and not at all when the text stays the same.

Parameters:

text – text for inserting, type (bytes or unicode) must match the text in the caption

>>> e = IntEdit("", 0)
>>> e.insert_text("7")
>>> e
<IntEdit selectable flow widget '7' edit_pos=1>
keypress(size: tuple[int], key: str) → str | None¶

Handle editing keystrokes. Remove leading zeros.

A digit is refused when the resulting text would exceed sys.get_int_max_str_digits() digits, so that value() can convert whatever the user typed.

>>> e, size = IntEdit("", 5002), (10,)
>>> e.keypress(size, "home")
>>> e.keypress(size, "delete")
>>> print(e.edit_text)
002
>>> e.keypress(size, "end")
>>> print(e.edit_text)
2
valid_char(ch: str) → bool¶

Return true for decimal digits.

value() → int¶

Return the numeric value of self.edit_text.

>>> e, size = IntEdit(), (10,)
>>> e.keypress(size, "5")
>>> e.keypress(size, "1")
>>> e.value() == 51
True
Raises:

ValueError – the text was set programmatically to something that is not a decimal integer, or to more digits than sys.get_int_max_str_digits() allows.

TreeWidget¶

class urwid.TreeWidget(node: _Node)¶

A widget representing something in a nested tree display.

Build the widget representing node, expanded as is_initially_expanded() says.

Deprecated since version 4.0.4: Passing a node that is not a ParentNode but defines get_first_child is deprecated.

collapse() → None¶

Hide the children of this node and update the icon.

A leaf has no children and no icon, so nothing changes for it. A descendant in focus keeps the focus although it is hidden. Move the focus first, for example with TreeListBox.move_focus_to_parent().

expand() → None¶

Show the children of this node and update the icon.

A leaf has no children and no icon, so nothing changes for it.

first_child() → TreeWidget[TreeNode[Any]] | None¶

Return first child if expanded.

get_display_text() → _TagMarkup¶

Return the text to display for this node, combining its key and value.

get_indent_cols() → int¶

Return the number of columns this widget is indented by, based on its node’s depth.

get_indented_widget() → Padding[Text | Columns]¶

Return this node’s widget wrapped with the expand/collapse icon and indentation.

get_inner_widget() → Text¶

Return the cached inner widget, creating it with load_inner_widget() if necessary.

get_node() → _Node¶

Return the TreeNode this widget represents.

is_initially_expanded() → bool¶

Return whether the widget starts expanded.

The default starts every node expanded. Override it to start collapsed, for example below a given depth. It is called from __init__ once the node is set, before the display widget is built.

keypress(size: tuple[int] | tuple[()], key: str) → str | None¶

Handle expand & collapse requests (non-leaf nodes).

last_child() → TreeWidget[TreeNode[Any]] | None¶

Return the last visible descendant if expanded.

The descent is a loop rather than a recursion, so the depth of the tree is not limited by the interpreter’s recursion limit. A descendant widget whose class overrides this method is asked for its own last descendant.

Raises:

TreeWidgetError – the descent reaches a node it already passed, so the tree has a cycle.

load_inner_widget() → Text¶

Create the inner widget displaying this node’s text.

mouse_event(size: tuple[int] | tuple[()], event: str, button: int, col: int, row: int, focus: bool) → bool¶

Toggle expand/collapse when the icon is left-clicked.

next_inorder() → TreeWidget[TreeNode[Any]] | None¶

Return the next TreeWidget depth first from this one.

Raises:

ValueError – the tree walker returned a node at an unexpected depth.

prev_inorder() → TreeWidget[TreeNode[Any]] | None¶

Return the previous TreeWidget depth first from this one.

selectable() → bool¶

Allow selection of non-leaf nodes so children may be (un)expanded.

toggle_expanded() → None¶

Switch this node between expanded and collapsed.

Nothing changes for a leaf.

update_expanded_icon() → None¶

Update display widget text for parent widgets.

Extended Numerical Editing Classes¶

IntegerEdit¶

class urwid.numedit.IntegerEdit(caption: _TagMarkup = '', default: int | str | decimal.Decimal | None = None, base: int = 10, *, allow_negative: bool = False)¶

Edit widget for integer values.

Initialize an edit widget restricted to integer values.

Parameters:

  • caption – caption markup

  • default – default edit value

  • base – the numeric base of the value, from 2 to 36

  • allow_negative – accept a leading minus sign in string defaults and input

Raises:

ValueError – default is not an int, str or integral decimal.Decimal, or does not consist of digits valid for base.

>>> IntegerEdit("", 42)
<IntegerEdit selectable flow widget '42' edit_pos=2>
>>> e, size = IntegerEdit("", "5002"), (10,)
>>> e.keypress(size, "home")
>>> e.keypress(size, "delete")
>>> assert e.edit_text == "002"
>>> e.keypress(size, "end")
>>> assert e.edit_text == "2"
>>> e.keypress(size, "9")
>>> e.keypress(size, "0")
>>> assert e.edit_text == "290"
>>> e, size = IntegerEdit("", ""), (10,)
>>> assert e.value() is None
>>> # binary
>>> e, size = IntegerEdit("", "1010", base=2), (10,)
>>> e.keypress(size, "end")
>>> e.keypress(size, "1")
>>> assert e.edit_text == "10101"
>>> assert e.value() == decimal.Decimal("21")
>>> # HEX
>>> e, size = IntegerEdit("", "10", base=16), (10,)
>>> e.keypress(size, "end")
>>> e.keypress(size, "F")
>>> e.keypress(size, "f")
>>> assert e.edit_text == "10Ff"
>>> assert e.keypress(size, "G") == "G"  # unhandled key
>>> assert e.edit_text == "10Ff"
>>> # keep leading 0's when not base 10
>>> e, size = IntegerEdit("", "10FF", base=16), (10,)
>>> assert e.edit_text == "10FF"
>>> assert e.value() == decimal.Decimal("4351")
>>> e.keypress(size, "home")
>>> e.keypress(size, "delete")
>>> e.keypress(size, "0")
>>> assert e.edit_text == "00FF"
>>> # test exception on incompatible value for base
>>> e, size = IntegerEdit("", "10FG", base=16), (10,)
Traceback (most recent call last):
    ...
ValueError: invalid value: 10FG for base 16
>>> # test exception on float init value
>>> e, size = IntegerEdit("", 10.0), (10,)
Traceback (most recent call last):
    ...
ValueError: default: Only 'str', 'int', 'long' or Decimal input allowed
>>> e, size = IntegerEdit("", decimal.Decimal("10.0")), (10,)
Traceback (most recent call last):
    ...
ValueError: not an 'integer Decimal' instance
value() → Decimal | None¶

Return the numeric value of self.edit_text.

>>> e, size = IntegerEdit(), (10,)
>>> e.keypress(size, "5")
>>> e.keypress(size, "1")
>>> assert e.value() == 51

FloatEdit¶

class urwid.numedit.FloatEdit(caption: _TagMarkup = '', default: str | int | decimal.Decimal | None = None, preserveSignificance: bool | None = None, decimalSeparator: str | None = None, *, preserve_significance: bool = True, decimal_separator: str = '.', allow_negative: bool = False)¶

Edit widget for float values.

Initialize a decimal edit widget.

Parameters:

  • caption – caption markup

  • default – default edit value. Strings must use the configured decimal separator.

  • preserveSignificance – deprecated positional form of preserve_significance

  • decimalSeparator – deprecated positional form of decimal_separator

  • preserve_significance – return value has the same signif. as default

  • decimal_separator – use ‘.’ as separator by default, optionally a ‘,’

  • allow_negative – accept a leading minus sign in string defaults and input

Raises:

ValueError – default is not an int, str or decimal.Decimal. default is a string with the other decimal separator, is not a number, or is not a finite value. decimal_separator is neither '.' nor ','.

Deprecated since version 2.2.3: The preserveSignificance and decimalSeparator arguments are deprecated, use the preserve_significance and decimal_separator keyword arguments instead. The arguments will be removed in version 7.0.

>>> FloatEdit("", "1.065434")
<FloatEdit selectable flow widget '1.065434' edit_pos=8>
>>> e, size = FloatEdit("", "1.065434"), (10,)
>>> e.keypress(size, "home")
>>> e.keypress(size, "delete")
>>> assert e.edit_text == ".065434"
>>> e.keypress(size, "end")
>>> e.keypress(size, "backspace")
>>> assert e.edit_text == ".06543"
>>> e, size = FloatEdit(), (10,)
>>> e.keypress(size, "5")
>>> e.keypress(size, "1")
>>> e.keypress(size, ".")
>>> e.keypress(size, "5")
>>> e.keypress(size, "1")
>>> assert e.value() == decimal.Decimal("51.51"), e.value()
>>> e, size = FloatEdit(decimal_separator=":"), (10,)
Traceback (most recent call last):
    ...
ValueError: invalid decimal separator: :
>>> e, size = FloatEdit(decimal_separator=","), (10,)
>>> e.keypress(size, "5")
>>> e.keypress(size, "1")
>>> e.keypress(size, ",")
>>> e.keypress(size, "5")
>>> e.keypress(size, "1")
>>> assert e.edit_text == "51,51"
>>> e, size = FloatEdit("", "3.1415", preserve_significance=True), (10,)
>>> e.keypress(size, "end")
>>> e.keypress(size, "backspace")
>>> e.keypress(size, "backspace")
>>> assert e.edit_text == "3.14"
>>> assert e.value() == decimal.Decimal("3.1400")
>>> e.keypress(size, "1")
>>> e.keypress(size, "5")
>>> e.keypress(size, "9")
>>> assert e.value() == decimal.Decimal("3.1416"), e.value()
>>> e, size = FloatEdit("", ""), (10,)
>>> assert e.value() is None
>>> e, size = FloatEdit("", 10.0), (10,)
Traceback (most recent call last):
    ...
ValueError: default: Only 'str', 'int', 'long' or Decimal input allowed
valid_char(ch: str) → bool¶

Return true for allowed characters, refusing a second decimal separator.

value() → Decimal | None¶

Return the numeric value of self.edit_text.

Control Widget Classes¶

Button¶

class urwid.Button(label: _TagMarkup, on_press: Callable[[Self, _T], Any] | None = None, user_data: _T = ..., *, align: Literal['left', 'center', 'right'] | Align = ..., wrap: Literal['space', 'any', 'clip', 'ellipsis'] | WrapMode = ..., layout: TextLayout | None = ..., cursor_position: int | None = ..., left: _TagMarkup | None = ..., right: _TagMarkup | None = ...)¶
class urwid.Button(label: _TagMarkup, on_press: Callable[[Self], Any] | None = None, user_data: None = None, *, align: Literal['left', 'center', 'right'] | Align = ..., wrap: Literal['space', 'any', 'clip', 'ellipsis'] | WrapMode = ..., layout: TextLayout | None = ..., cursor_position: int | None = ..., left: _TagMarkup | None = ..., right: _TagMarkup | None = ...)

Selectable widget that emits a click signal when activated.

Create the Button widget.

Parameters:

  • label – markup for button label

  • on_press – shorthand for connect_signal() function call for a single callback

  • user_data – user_data for on_press

  • align – typically 'left', 'center' or 'right'

  • wrap – typically 'space', 'any', 'clip' or 'ellipsis'

  • layout – defaults to a shared StandardTextLayout instance

  • cursor_position – position of the cursor in the label when the button is in focus; None shows no cursor, see SelectableIcon

  • left – markup for the left bracket, in a column as wide as its text; None uses button_left in a column of width 1, and markup with no text leaves out the bracket together with the space after it

  • right – markup for the right bracket, the same way as left with button_right

..note:: pack method expect, that Columns backend widget is not modified from outside

Signals supported: 'click'

Register signal handler with:

urwid.connect_signal(button, "click", callback, user_data)

where callback is callback(button [,user_data]) Unregister signal handlers with:

urwid.disconnect_signal(button, "click", callback, user_data)

>>> from urwid.util import set_temporary_encoding
>>> Button("Ok")
<Button selectable fixed/flow widget 'Ok'>
>>> b = Button("Cancel")
>>> b.render((15,), focus=True).text  # ... = b in Python 3
[b'< Cancel      >']
>>> aligned_button = Button("Test", align=Align.CENTER)
>>> aligned_button.render((10,), focus=True).text
[b'<  Test  >']
>>> wrapped_button = Button("Long label", wrap=WrapMode.ELLIPSIS)
>>> with set_temporary_encoding("utf-8"):
...     wrapped_button.render((7,), focus=False).text[0].decode("utf-8")
'< Lo… >'
>>> Button("Ok", left="[[", right="]]").render((8,)).text
[b'[[ Ok ]]']
>>> Button("Link", left="", right="").render((4,)).text
[b'Link']
>>> Button("Ok", cursor_position=None).render((6,), focus=True).cursor
get_label() → str | bytes¶

Return label text.

>>> b = Button("Ok")
>>> print(b.get_label())
Ok
>>> print(b.label)
Ok
keypress(size: tuple[int], key: str) → str | None¶

Send ‘click’ signal on ‘activate’ command.

>>> assert Button._command_map[" "] == "activate"
>>> assert Button._command_map["enter"] == "activate"
>>> size = (15,)
>>> b = Button("Cancel")
>>> clicked_buttons = []
>>> def handle_click(button):
...     clicked_buttons.append(button.label)
>>> key = connect_signal(b, "click", handle_click)
>>> b.keypress(size, "enter")
>>> b.keypress(size, " ")
>>> clicked_buttons
['Cancel', 'Cancel']
property label: str | bytes¶

Return label text.

>>> b = Button("Ok")
>>> print(b.get_label())
Ok
>>> print(b.label)
Ok
mouse_event(size: tuple[int], event: str, button: int, col: int, row: int, focus: bool) → bool¶

Send ‘click’ signal on button 1 press.

>>> size = (15,)
>>> b = Button("Ok")
>>> clicked_buttons = []
>>> def handle_click(button):
...     clicked_buttons.append(button.label)
>>> key = connect_signal(b, "click", handle_click)
>>> b.mouse_event(size, "mouse press", 1, 4, 0, True)
True
>>> b.mouse_event(size, "mouse press", 2, 4, 0, True)  # ignored
False
>>> clicked_buttons
['Ok']
pack(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | None = (), focus: bool = False) → tuple[int, int]¶

Pack for widget.

Parameters:

  • size – size data. Special case: () - get minimal widget size to fit

  • focus – widget is focused

Returns:

the (columns, rows) the widget needs.

>>> btn = Button("Some button")
>>> btn.pack((10,))
(10, 2)
>>> btn.pack()
(15, 1)
>>> btn.pack((), True)
(15, 1)
set_label(label: _TagMarkup) → None¶

Change the button label.

Parameters:

label – markup for button label

>>> b = Button("Ok")
>>> b.set_label("Yup yup")
>>> b
<Button selectable fixed/flow widget 'Yup yup'>

CheckBox¶

class urwid.CheckBox(label: _TagMarkup, state: bool = False, has_mixed: Literal[False] = False, on_state_change: Callable[[Self, bool, _T], Any] | None = None, user_data: _T = ..., checked_symbol: str | None = ...)¶
class urwid.CheckBox(label: _TagMarkup, state: Literal['mixed'] | bool = False, has_mixed: Literal[True] = True, on_state_change: Callable[[Self, bool | Literal['mixed'], _T], Any] | None = None, user_data: _T = ..., checked_symbol: str | None = ...)
class urwid.CheckBox(label: _TagMarkup, state: bool = False, has_mixed: Literal[False] = False, on_state_change: Callable[[Self, bool], Any] | None = None, user_data: None = None, checked_symbol: str | None = ...)
class urwid.CheckBox(label: _TagMarkup, state: Literal['mixed'] | bool = False, has_mixed: Literal[True] = True, on_state_change: Callable[[Self, bool | Literal['mixed']], Any] | None = None, user_data: None = None, checked_symbol: str | None = ...)

Selectable widget that toggles between checked, unchecked, and mixed states.

Create the CheckBox widget.

Parameters:

  • label – markup for check box label

  • state – False, True or “mixed”

  • has_mixed – True if “mixed” is a state to cycle through

  • on_state_change – shorthand for connect_signal() function call for a single callback

  • user_data – user_data for on_state_change

  • checked_symbol – the symbol drawn inside the brackets for the checked state, None for the default one

Raises:

ValueError – state is not one of the states of this check box.

..note:: pack method expect, that Columns backend widget is not modified from outside

Signals supported: 'change', "postchange"

Register signal handler with:

urwid.connect_signal(check_box, "change", callback, user_data)

where callback is callback(check_box, new_state [,user_data]) Unregister signal handlers with:

urwid.disconnect_signal(check_box, "change", callback, user_data)

>>> CheckBox("Confirm")
<CheckBox selectable fixed/flow widget 'Confirm' state=False>
>>> CheckBox("Yogourt", "mixed", True)

[b'[X] Extra onions    ']

set_state(state: bool | Literal['mixed'], do_callback: bool = True) → None¶

Set the CheckBox state.

Parameters:

  • state – True, False or “mixed”

  • do_callback – False to suppress signal from this change

Raises:

CheckBoxError – state is not one of the states of this check box.

>>> from urwid import disconnect_signal
>>> changes = []
>>> def callback_a(user_data, cb, state):
...     changes.append("A %r %r" % (state, user_data))
>>> def callback_b(cb, state):
...     changes.append("B %r" % state)
>>> cb = CheckBox("test", False, False)
>>> key1 = connect_signal(cb, "change", callback_a, user_args=("user_a",))
>>> key2 = connect_signal(cb, "change", callback_b)
>>> cb.set_state(True)  # both callbacks will be triggered
>>> cb.state
True
>>> disconnect_signal(cb, "change", callback_a, user_args=("user_a",))
>>> cb.state = False
>>> cb.state
False
>>> cb.set_state(True)
>>> cb.state
True
>>> cb.set_state(False, False)  # don't send signal
>>> changes
["A True 'user_a'", 'B True', 'B False', 'B True']

Cycle to the next valid state.

>>> cb = CheckBox("3-state", has_mixed=True)
>>> cb.state
False
>>> cb.toggle_state()
>>> cb.state
True
>>> cb.toggle_state()
>>> cb.state
'mixed'
>>> cb.toggle_state()
>>> cb.state

RadioButton¶

class urwid.RadioButton(group: MutableSequence[RadioButton], label: _TagMarkup, state: bool | Literal['first True'] = ..., on_state_change: Callable[[Self, bool, _T], Any] | None = None, user_data: _T = ...)¶
class urwid.RadioButton(group: MutableSequence[RadioButton], label: _TagMarkup, state: bool | Literal['first True'] = ..., on_state_change: Callable[[Self, bool], Any] | None = None, user_data: None = None)

Checkbox-like widget that exclusively selects itself within a shared group list.

Create the RadioButton widget.

Parameters:

  • group – list for radio buttons in same group

  • label – markup for radio button label

  • state – False, True, “mixed” or “first True”

  • on_state_change – shorthand for connect_signal() function call for a single ‘change’ callback

  • user_data – user_data for on_state_change

..note:: pack method expect, that Columns backend widget is not modified from outside

This function will append the new radio button to group. “first True” will set to True if group is empty.

Signals supported: 'change', "postchange"

Register signal handler with:

urwid.connect_signal(radio_button, "change", callback, user_data)

where callback is callback(radio_button, new_state [,user_data]) Unregister signal handlers with:

urwid.disconnect_signal(radio_button, "change", callback, user_data)

>>> bgroup = []  # button group
>>> b1 = RadioButton(bgroup, "Agree")
>>> b2 = RadioButton(bgroup, "Disagree")
>>> len(bgroup)
2
>>> b1
<RadioButton selectable fixed/flow widget 'Agree' state=True>
>>> b2
<RadioButton selectable fixed/flow widget 'Disagree' state=False>
>>> b2.render((15,), focus=True).text  # ... = b in Python 3
[...'( ) Disagree   ']
set_state(state: bool | Literal['mixed'], do_callback: bool = True) → None¶

Set the RadioButton state.

Parameters:

  • state – True, False or “mixed”

  • do_callback – False to suppress signal from this change

If state is True all other radio buttons in the same button group will be set to False.

>>> bgroup = []  # button group
>>> b1 = RadioButton(bgroup, "Agree")
>>> b2 = RadioButton(bgroup, "Disagree")
>>> b3 = RadioButton(bgroup, "Unsure")
>>> b1.state, b2.state, b3.state
(True, False, False)
>>> b2.set_state(True)
>>> b1.state, b2.state, b3.state
(False, True, False)
>>> def relabel_button(radio_button, new_state):
...     radio_button.set_label("Think Harder!")
>>> key = connect_signal(b3, "change", relabel_button)
>>> b3
<RadioButton selectable fixed/flow widget 'Unsure' state=False>
>>> b3.set_state(True)  # this will trigger the callback
>>> b3
<RadioButton selectable fixed/flow widget 'Think Harder!' state=True>
property state: bool | Literal['mixed']¶

Return the state of the checkbox.

toggle_state() → None¶

Set state to True.

>>> bgroup = []  # button group
>>> b1 = RadioButton(bgroup, "Agree")
>>> b2 = RadioButton(bgroup, "Disagree")
>>> b1.state, b2.state
(True, False)
>>> b2.toggle_state()
>>> b1.state, b2.state
(False, True)
>>> b2.toggle_state()
>>> b1.state, b2.state
(False, True)

DropDown¶

class urwid.DropDown(options: Iterable[_TagMarkup], *, selected: int = 0, max_visible_items: int = 10, attr_map: Hashable | Mapping[Hashable, Hashable] = None, focus_map: Hashable | Mapping[Hashable, Hashable] = None)¶

Drop-down choice: shows the selected option, and on activation opens a list of all options below it.

The list opens with the selected option focused. It moves above the widget when it does not fit below, and when it fits on neither side it takes the side with more rows and scrolls. enter, space or a click chooses the focused option and closes the list; esc closes it without a change.

Important

DropDown requires MainLoop(..., pop_ups=True), or another PopUpTarget above it. The list is a pop-up, and without a target activating the widget shows nothing.

Signals supported: 'change', sent as callback(drop_down, new_index) before selected changes, so the callback still reads the previous value there.

>>> drop_down = DropDown(["red", "green", "blue"], selected=1)
>>> drop_down.render(()).text
[b'green v']
>>> drop_down.selected = 2
>>> drop_down.render((10,)).text
[b'blue     v']

Create a drop-down over options, with the option at index selected shown.

Parameters:

  • options – markup of each option, in list order; see Text for markup.

  • selected – index of the option shown first.

  • max_visible_items – most options the open list shows at once; it scrolls through the rest.

  • attr_map – display attribute of each option in the open list, as for AttrMap.

  • focus_map – display attribute of the focused option in the open list.

Raises:

  • ValueError – options is empty, or max_visible_items is less than 1.

  • IndexError – selected is not an index of options.

create_pop_up() → ScrollBar[ListBox[int]]¶

Return the list of all options, with the selected one focused; it scrolls when they do not all fit.

drop_down_indicator: ClassVar[Text] = <Text fixed/flow widget 'v'>¶

Widget drawn after the selected option; a subclass replaces it to change the indicator.

get_pop_up_parameters() → PopUpParametersModel¶

Return the list position directly below this widget, anchored to it so it can move above it.

keypress(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], key: str) → str | None¶

Open the list on the activate command.

mouse_event(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], event: str, button: int, col: int, row: int, focus: bool) → bool¶

Open the list on a button 1 press.

property options: tuple[_TagMarkup, ...]¶

Markup of each option, in list order.

pack(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int] = (), focus: bool = False) → tuple[int, int]¶

Return the size of this widget; with no size, as wide as the widest option.

render(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → CompositeCanvas | Canvas¶

Render the selected option and the indicator, with the list attached when it is open.

property selected: int¶

Index of the selected option.

Setting it sends the 'change' signal when the index differs from the current one.

Raises:

IndexError – the new value is not an index of options.

ANSIText¶

class urwid.ANSIText(ansi_text: str, previous_attr: AttrSpec | ParsedLine | ANSIText | None = None, *, one_line: bool = False, wrap: Literal['space', 'any', 'clip', 'ellipsis'] | WrapMode = WrapMode.SPACE, align: Literal['left', 'center', 'right'] | Align = Align.LEFT)¶

A read-only widget interpreting ANSI/VT100 colour, horizontal and (optionally) vertical movement escapes.

It acts almost exactly like a read-only Text widget for the resolved, escape-free content.

Parsing is delegated to urwid.ansi_parser.AnsiParser, and layout (wrapping, alignment, packing and rendering) is delegated to an internal Text instance that this widget wraps via WidgetWrap, so this widget’s pack/render/rows behaviour is identical to Text for the same resolved characters, without needing to forward those calls by hand.

By default (one_line=False), a newline genuinely starts a new row, CSI n A/B genuinely moves the cursor up/down between rows, and a bare \r genuinely overwrites the current row in place (letting progress-bar-style redraw sequences resolve correctly) – ansi_text is treated as a single, complete block, meant to render one already-complete captured screen/block.

Pass one_line=True to restrict this widget to a single physical line of resolved text; see AnsiParser’s one_line flag for the underlying parsing semantics. In this mode, line ends and vertical cursor movement are treated as meaningless outside a single line (stripped/split rather than resolved into rows): since the underlying parser always returns a tuple[ParsedLine, ...] in this mode (line ends, VT and FF outside an OSC string are structural split points, never silently discarded), constructing an ANSIText directly from text containing an embedded line end only surfaces the first resulting line – no data is lost (the full split is always computed), but only the first line is exposed by this widget instance. Use from_lines() to turn arbitrary multi-line (or arbitrarily chunked) raw text into a complete sequence of ANSIText instances, in either mode.

>>> ANSIText("hello")
<ANSIText fixed/flow widget 'hello'>
>>> ANSIText("a\nb").text
'a\nb'
>>> ANSIText("a\nb", one_line=True).text
'a'

Build the widget from a block of ANSI/VT100-escaped text.

Parameters:

  • ansi_text – a block of text, optionally spanning several lines and containing ANSI/VT100 escape sequences. If one_line is true, only its first physical line is surfaced by this widget instance.

  • previous_attr – SGR/colour state to carry in from previously parsed text (see last_attr), or the ANSIText or ParsedLine of that text, to carry its character sets in as well.

  • one_line – restrict this widget to a single physical line of resolved text rather than resolving the whole block into multi-row output.

  • wrap – forwarded to the internal Text.

  • align – forwarded to the internal Text.

property attrib: list[tuple[Hashable, int]]¶

Read-only property returning the run-length encoded display attributes of this widget’s text.

property bel: int¶

The number of BEL characters seen (aggregated over the whole block unless one_line is true).

classmethod from_lines(chunks: Iterable[str], previous_attr: AttrSpec | ParsedLine | ANSIText | None = None, *, one_line: bool = False, **kwargs: Any) → Iterator[ANSIText]¶

Consume raw ANSI text chunks and yield the resulting ANSIText widget(s).

chunks (e.g. successive os.read() results from a subprocess) are not required to be pre-split on line boundaries, and each chunk may contain zero, one, or several line ends. Internally accumulates a single AnsiParser across all chunks, so a line split across two chunk boundaries – or an escape sequence split across two chunk boundaries – is still resolved correctly, and calls finalize() only once the iterable is exhausted.

If one_line is true, one ANSIText is yielded per line the shared parser completes, in order, with SGR colour state and character sets carried forward continuously: each produced ANSIText continues from the previous one, whether that previous line came from the same chunk or an earlier one.

If one_line is false (the default), this naturally reduces to yielding exactly one ANSIText once every chunk has been consumed, representing the entire accumulated multi-chunk block resolved into real multi-row output – the “normal multiline” case, reached through the same code path as the one_line=True case rather than a separate one.

Parameters:

  • chunks – an iterable of raw text chunks, not required to be aligned on line or escape-sequence boundaries.

  • previous_attr – SGR/colour state to seed the shared parser with, as if it were carried over from previously parsed text, or the ANSIText or ParsedLine of that text, to carry its character sets in as well.

  • one_line – parse in single-line-splitting mode (see the class docstring) rather than resolving the whole accumulated input into one multi-row block.

  • kwargs – forwarded to _from_parsed() (i.e. wrap/align for the internal Text).

Yields:

one or more ANSIText instances, in order, depending on one_line.

get_text() → tuple[str | bytes, list[tuple[Hashable, int]]]¶

Return (text, display attributes), see urwid.Text.get_text().

property last_attr: AttrSpec | None¶

The SGR/colour state in effect at the very end of this widget’s text.

Feed this in as previous_attr to a subsequently constructed ANSIText to continue the same colour state; feed this widget itself instead to continue the character sets (such as the DEC Special Graphics line drawing) as well.

property leds: str | None¶

The last keyboard-LED state requested, if any.

set_ansi_text(ansi_text: str, previous_attr: AttrSpec | ParsedLine | ANSIText | None = None) → None¶

Re-parse ansi_text and invalidate this widget.

Parsing uses the mode (one_line) this widget was constructed with; if one_line is true, only the first resulting line is used, see the class docstring.

Parameters:

  • ansi_text – a block of text, optionally spanning several lines and containing ANSI/VT100 escape sequences.

  • previous_attr – SGR/colour state to carry in from previously parsed text (see last_attr), or the ANSIText or ParsedLine of that text, to carry its character sets in as well.

property text: str | bytes¶

Read-only property returning the resolved, escape-free text of this widget (may contain \n).

property title: str | None¶

The last OSC window-title string seen, if any.

Decoration Widget Classes¶

AttrMap¶

class urwid.AttrMap(w: WrappedWidget, attr_map: Hashable | Mapping[Hashable, Hashable], focus_map: Hashable | Mapping[Hashable, Hashable] = None)¶

A decoration that maps one set of display attributes to another.

This object will pass all function calls and variable references to the wrapped widget.

Parameters:

  • w – widget to wrap (stored as self.original_widget)

  • attr_map – attribute to apply to w, or dict of old display attribute: new display attribute mappings; the other attributes of w are placed over the attribute of None, so their ‘inherit’ colors are taken from it (see LayeredAttr), and an attribute mapped to None shows the attribute of None

  • focus_map – attribute to apply when in focus or dict of old display attribute: new display attribute mappings; if None use attr

>>> from urwid import Divider, Edit, Text
>>> AttrMap(Divider("!"), "bright")
<AttrMap flow widget <Divider flow widget '!'> attr_map={None: 'bright'}>
>>> AttrMap(Edit(), "notfocus", "focus").attr_map
{None: 'notfocus'}
>>> AttrMap(Edit(), "notfocus", "focus").focus_map
{None: 'focus'}
>>> size = (5,)
>>> am = AttrMap(Text("hi"), "greeting", "fgreet")
>>> next(am.render(size, focus=False).content())  # ... = b in Python 3
[('greeting', None, ...'hi   ')]
>>> next(am.render(size, focus=True).content())
[('fgreet', None, ...'hi   ')]
>>> am2 = AttrMap(Text(("word", "hi")), {"word": "greeting", None: "bg"})
>>> am2
<AttrMap fixed/flow widget <Text fixed/flow widget 'hi'> attr_map={'word': 'greeting', None: 'bg'}>
>>> next(am2.render(size).content())
[(LayeredAttr('greeting', 'bg'), None, ...'hi'), ('bg', None, ...'   ')]
property attr_map: dict[Hashable, Hashable]¶

Return a copy of the attribute mapping dictionary.

property focus_map: dict[Hashable, Hashable] | None¶

Return a copy of the focus attribute mapping dictionary, or None if unset.

get_attr_map() → dict[Hashable, Hashable]¶

Return a copy of the attribute mapping dictionary.

get_focus_map() → dict[Hashable, Hashable] | None¶

Return a copy of the focus attribute mapping dictionary, or None if unset.

render(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → CompositeCanvas¶

Render wrapped widget and apply attribute. Return canvas.

set_attr_map(attr_map: Hashable | Mapping[Hashable, Hashable]) → None¶

Set the attribute mapping dictionary {from_attr: to_attr, …}.

A single attribute is stored as {None: attribute}, the way the constructor does.

>>> from urwid import Text
>>> w = AttrMap(Text("hi"), None)
>>> w.set_attr_map({"a": "b"})
>>> w
<AttrMap fixed/flow widget <Text fixed/flow widget 'hi'> attr_map={'a': 'b'}>
>>> w.set_attr_map("c")
>>> w
<AttrMap fixed/flow widget <Text fixed/flow widget 'hi'> attr_map={None: 'c'}>
Raises:

AttrMapError – a key or value of the mapping is not hashable.

set_focus_map(focus_map: Hashable | Mapping[Hashable, Hashable] | None) → None¶

Set the focus attribute mapping dictionary {from_attr: to_attr, …}.

If None this widget will use the attr mapping instead (no change when in focus).

A single attribute is stored as {None: attribute}, the way the constructor does.

>>> from urwid import Text
>>> w = AttrMap(Text("hi"), {})
>>> w.set_focus_map({"a": "b"})
>>> w
<AttrMap fixed/flow widget <Text fixed/flow widget 'hi'> attr_map={} focus_map={'a': 'b'}>
>>> w.set_focus_map("c")
>>> w
<AttrMap fixed/flow widget <Text fixed/flow widget 'hi'> attr_map={} focus_map={None: 'c'}>
>>> w.set_focus_map(None)
>>> w
<AttrMap fixed/flow widget <Text fixed/flow widget 'hi'> attr_map={}>
Raises:

AttrMapError – a key or value of the mapping is not hashable.

Padding¶

class urwid.Padding(w: WrappedWidget, align: Literal['left', 'center', 'right'] | Align | tuple[Literal['relative', WHSettings.RELATIVE, 'fixed left', 'fixed right'], int] = Align.LEFT, width: int | Literal['pack', 'clip', WHSettings.PACK, WHSettings.CLIP] | tuple[Literal['relative', WHSettings.RELATIVE, 'fixed left', 'fixed right'], int] | None = (WHSettings.RELATIVE, 100), min_width: int | None = None, left: int = 0, right: int = 0)¶

Decoration that adds blank columns to the left and/or right of a wrapped widget.

Build the widget, padding w on the left and/or right.

Parameters:

  • w – a box, flow or fixed widget to pad on the left and/or right this widget is stored as self.original_widget

  • align – one of: 'left', 'center', 'right' ('relative', percentage 0=left 100=right)

  • width –

    one of:

    given width

    integer number of columns for self.original_widget

    'pack'

    try to pack self.original_widget to its ideal size

    ('relative', percentage of total width)

    make width depend on the container’s width

    'clip'

    to enable clipping mode for a fixed widget

  • min_width – the minimum number of columns for self.original_widget or None

  • left – a fixed number of columns to pad on the left

  • right – a fixed number of columns to pad on the right

Clipping Mode: (width= 'clip') In clipping mode this padding widget will behave as a flow widget and self.original_widget will be treated as a fixed widget. self.original_widget will be clipped to fit the available number of columns. For example if align is 'left' then self.original_widget may be clipped on the right.

Pack Mode: (width= 'pack') In pack mode is supported FIXED operation if it is supported by the original widget.

>>> from urwid import Divider, Text, BigText, FontRegistry
>>> from urwid.util import set_temporary_encoding
>>> size = (7,)
>>> def pr(w):
...     with set_temporary_encoding("utf-8"):
...         for t in w.render(size).text:
...             print(f"|{t.decode('utf-8')}|")
>>> pr(Padding(Text("Head"), ("relative", 20), "pack"))
| Head  |
>>> pr(Padding(Divider("-"), left=2, right=1))
|  ---- |
>>> pr(Padding(Divider("*"), "center", 3))
|  ***  |
>>> p = Padding(Text("1234"), "left", 2, None, 1, 1)
>>> p
<Padding fixed/flow widget <Text fixed/flow widget '1234'> left=1 right=1 width=2>
>>> pr(p)  # align against left
| 12    |
| 34    |
>>> p.align = "right"
>>> pr(p)  # align against right
|    12 |
|    34 |
>>> pr(Padding(Text("hi\nthere"), "right", "pack"))  # pack text first
|  hi   |
|  there|
>>> pr(Padding(BigText("1,2,3", FontRegistry["Thin 3x3"]()), width="clip"))
| ┐  ┌─┐|
| │  ┌─┘|
| ┴ ,└─ |
property align: Literal['left', 'center', 'right'] | Align | tuple[Literal['relative', WHSettings.RELATIVE], int]¶

Return the padding alignment setting.

Raises:

PaddingError – this Padding uses CLIP, which makes it FLOW-only, or its width type does not resolve to a fixed size.

Warns PaddingWarning:

the wrapped widget does not support the sizing a FIXED pack needs: FLOW for a GIVEN width, FIXED otherwise.

padding_values(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], focus: bool) → tuple[int, int]¶

Return the number of columns to pad on the left and right.

Override this method to define custom padding behaviour.

Raises:

PaddingError – this Padding uses CLIP and no size was given.

render(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → CompositeCanvas¶

Render the Padding and return the resulting canvas.

Raises:

ValueError – the Padding is empty and no size was given.

Warns PaddingWarning:

the width is GIVEN and size is too narrow for it.

rows(size: tuple[int], focus: bool = False) → int¶

Return the rows needed for self.original_widget.

sizing() → frozenset[Sizing]¶

Widget sizing.

Rules: * width == CLIP: only FLOW is supported, and wrapped widget should support FIXED * width == GIVEN: FIXED is supported, and wrapped widget should support FLOW * All other cases: use sizing of target widget

Warns PaddingWarning:

the width is GIVEN and the wrapped widget supports neither FLOW nor BOX sizing.

property width: Literal[WHSettings.CLIP, WHSettings.PACK] | int | tuple[Literal[WHSettings.RELATIVE], int]¶

Return the padding width.

Filler¶

class urwid.Filler(body: WrappedWidget, valign: Literal['top', 'middle', 'bottom'] | VAlign | tuple[Literal['relative', 'fixed top', 'fixed bottom', WHSettings.RELATIVE], int] = VAlign.MIDDLE, height: int | Literal['pack', WHSettings.PACK] | tuple[Literal['relative', 'fixed top', 'fixed bottom', WHSettings.RELATIVE], int] | None = WHSettings.PACK, min_height: int | None = None, top: int = 0, bottom: int = 0)¶

Box widget decoration that vertically aligns a flow or box widget within the available space.

Parameters:

  • body – a flow widget or box widget to be filled around (stored as self.original_widget)

  • valign – one of: 'top', 'middle', 'bottom', ('relative', percentage 0=top 100=bottom)

  • height –

    one of:

    'pack'

    if body is a flow widget

    given height

    integer number of rows for self.original_widget

    ('relative', percentage of total height)

    make height depend on container’s height

  • min_height –

    one of:

    None

    if no minimum or if body is a flow widget

    minimum height

    integer number of rows for the widget when height not fixed

  • top – a fixed number of rows to fill at the top

  • bottom – a fixed number of rows to fill at the bottom

Raises:

FillerError – valign is not a vertical alignment value, or a fixed height is combined with a valign it cannot be used with.

If body is a flow widget, then height must be 'pack' and min_height will be ignored. Sizing of the filler will be BOX/FLOW in this case.

If height is integer, min_height will be ignored and sizing of filler will be BOX/FLOW.

Filler widgets will try to satisfy height argument first by reducing the valign amount when necessary. If height still cannot be satisfied it will also be reduced.

filler_values(size: tuple[int, int] | tuple[int], focus: bool) → tuple[int, int]¶

Return the number of rows to pad on the top and bottom.

Override this method to define custom padding behaviour.

get_cursor_coords(size: tuple[int, int] | tuple[int]) → tuple[int, int] | None¶

Return cursor coords from self.original_widget if any.

get_pref_col(size: tuple[int, int] | tuple[int]) → int | Literal['left', 'right', Align.LEFT, Align.RIGHT] | None¶

Return pref_col from self.original_widget if any.

keypress(size: tuple[int, int] | tuple[int], key: str) → str | None¶

Pass keypress to self.original_widget.

mouse_event(size: tuple[int, int] | tuple[int], event: str, button: int, col: int, row: int, focus: bool) → bool | None¶

Pass to self.original_widget.

move_cursor_to_coords(size: tuple[int, int] | tuple[int], col: int | Literal['left', 'right', Align.LEFT, Align.RIGHT], row: int) → bool¶

Pass to self.original_widget.

render(size: tuple[int, int] | tuple[int], focus: bool = False) → CompositeCanvas¶

Render self.original_widget with space above and/or below.

rows(size: tuple[int], focus: bool = False) → int¶

Flow pack support if FLOW sizing supported.

Raises:

FillerError – this Filler wraps a BOX widget, so it has no flow row count.

selectable() → bool¶

Return selectable from body.

sizing() → frozenset[Sizing]¶

Widget sizing.

Sizing BOX is always supported. Sizing FLOW is supported if: FLOW widget (a height type is PACK) or BOX widget with height GIVEN

Rules: * height == PACK: the height is taken from the wrapped widget, which therefore should support FLOW

Warns FillerWarning:

the height is PACK and the wrapped widget does not support FLOW sizing.

Symbols¶

alias of DividerSymbols

render(size: tuple[int], focus: bool = False) → CompositeCanvas¶

Render the divider as a canvas and return it.

>>> Divider().render((10,)).text  # ... = b in Python 3
[...'          ']
