LineBox¶

class urwid.LineBox(original_widget: WrappedWidget, title: _TagMarkup = '', title_align: Literal['left', 'center', 'right'] | Align = Align.CENTER, title_attr: Hashable = None, tlcorner: str = '┌', tline: str = '─', lline: str = '│', trcorner: str = '┐', blcorner: str = '└', rline: str = '│', bline: str = '─', brcorner: str = '┘')¶

Box widget decoration that draws a line border, with an optional title, around another widget.

Draw a line around original_widget.

Use ‘title’ to set an initial title text with will be centered on top of the box. It may be any text markup accepted by Text.

Use title_attr to apply a specific attribute to the title text.

Use title_align to align the title to the ‘left’, ‘right’, or ‘center’. The default is ‘center’.

You can also override the widgets used for the lines/corners:

tline: top line bline: bottom line lline: left line rline: right line tlcorner: top left corner trcorner: top right corner blcorner: bottom left corner brcorner: bottom right corner

If empty string is specified for one of the lines/corners, then no character will be output there. If no top/bottom/left/right lines - whole lines will be omitted. This allows for seamless use of adjoining LineBoxes.

Class attribute Symbols can be used as source for standard lines:

>>> print(LineBox(Text("Some text")).render(()))
┌─────────┐
│Some text│
└─────────┘
>>> print(
...     LineBox(
...         Text("Some text"),
...         tlcorner=LineBox.Symbols.LIGHT.TOP_LEFT_ROUNDED,
...         trcorner=LineBox.Symbols.LIGHT.TOP_RIGHT_ROUNDED,
...         blcorner=LineBox.Symbols.LIGHT.BOTTOM_LEFT_ROUNDED,
...         brcorner=LineBox.Symbols.LIGHT.BOTTOM_RIGHT_ROUNDED,
...     ).render(())
... )
╭─────────╮
│Some text│
╰─────────╯
>>> print(
...     LineBox(
...         Text("Some text"),
...         tline=LineBox.Symbols.HEAVY.HORIZONTAL,
...         bline=LineBox.Symbols.HEAVY.HORIZONTAL,
...         lline=LineBox.Symbols.HEAVY.VERTICAL,
...         rline=LineBox.Symbols.HEAVY.VERTICAL,
...         tlcorner=LineBox.Symbols.HEAVY.TOP_LEFT,
...         trcorner=LineBox.Symbols.HEAVY.TOP_RIGHT,
...         blcorner=LineBox.Symbols.HEAVY.BOTTOM_LEFT,
...         brcorner=LineBox.Symbols.HEAVY.BOTTOM_RIGHT,
...     ).render(())
... )
┏━━━━━━━━━┓
┃Some text┃
┗━━━━━━━━━┛

To make Table constructions, some lineboxes need to be drawn without sides and T or CROSS symbols used for corners of cells.

Raises:

ValueError – a title with text is given while tline is empty, or title_align is not a supported alignment.

property focus: AbstractWidget | None¶

LineBox is partially container.

While focus position is a bit hacky (formally it’s not container and only position 0 available), focus widget is always provided by original widget.

format_title(text: _TagMarkup) → _TagMarkup¶

Return text padded with spaces for display in the box’s top border, or an empty string if unset.

A string stays a string; other text markup is returned as the list [" ", text, " "]. Markup with no text, such as ("attr", ""), counts as unset.

property original_widget: WrappedWidget¶

Return the widget wrapped by the line box.

set_title(text: _TagMarkup) → None¶

Set the title shown in the top line of the box.

Raises:

ValueError – this LineBox has no top line to put a title on.

Pop-up Widget Classes¶

PopUpLauncher¶

class urwid.PopUpLauncher(original_widget: LauncherWidget, *, close_on_menu: bool = False)¶

Decoration that lets a wrapped widget open and close a pop-up drawn over other widgets by a PopUpTarget.

Wrap original_widget, with no pop-up open yet.

Parameters:

  • original_widget – widget that opens the pop-up.

  • close_on_menu – close the pop-up when it leaves a key for the menu command (esc by default) unhandled while it is the topmost open pop-up.

close_pop_up() → None¶

Discard the currently open pop-up widget, if any, and invalidate this widget.

create_pop_up() → AbstractWidget¶

Return the widget to be used for the pop-up.

Subclass must override this method. It is called once each time the pop-up is opened.

PopUpTarget renders the pop-up with the box size declared by get_pop_up_parameters(), so the widget returned here must accept an (overlay_width, overlay_height) size. Wrap a flow or fixed widget in a Filler (or in another box container) before returning it.

Raises:

NotImplementedError – the subclass does not override this method.

get_pop_up_parameters() → PopUpParametersModel¶

Return a dict of pop-up parameters.

For example: {'left': 0, 'top': 1, 'overlay_width': 30, 'overlay_height': 4, 'anchor_height': 1}.

Subclass must override this method. It is called each time this widget is rendered.

The optional anchor_height key makes PopUpTarget move the pop-up above the launcher, or clip its height, when it does not fit below; see CompositeCanvas.set_pop_up.

Raises:

NotImplementedError – the subclass does not override this method.

property launcher_size: tuple[int, int] | None¶

The (columns, rows) of the last render that was not served from the canvas cache, or None before it.

It is set before get_pop_up_parameters() is called, so inside that method it is always the size being rendered.

open_pop_up() → None¶

Create the pop-up widget via create_pop_up() and invalidate this widget.

property pop_up_widget: AbstractWidget | None¶

The open pop-up widget, or None when the pop-up is closed.

render(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → CompositeCanvas | Canvas¶

Render the wrapped widget, attaching the open pop-up widget to the canvas, if any.

PopUpTarget¶

class urwid.PopUpTarget(original_widget: WrappedWidget)¶

Box widget that overlays the pop-up(s) declared by a PopUpLauncher inside it.

Pop-ups nest: a pop-up widget may itself be a PopUpLauncher with its own pop-up open, in which case it is drawn overlaid on top of the pop-up that opened it, and so on for as many levels as are open at once.

Wrap original_widget, which is rendered with any open pop-up(s) overlaid on top.

Parameters:

original_widget – box widget to wrap; typically contains a PopUpLauncher.

enter_selectable(*, reverse: bool = False) → None¶

Do nothing: every focus under this widget is kept when a parent container enters it.

The widget that receives keys is known only after the pop-ups were laid out at the current size, which the entry hook does not have, see Moving the Focus with Tab.

get_cursor_coords(size: tuple[int, int]) → tuple[int, int] | None¶

Return the cursor coordinates of the current widget.

Raises:

TypeError – the current widget has no get_cursor_coords method.

get_pref_col(size: tuple[int, int]) → int | Literal['left', 'right', Align.LEFT, Align.RIGHT] | None¶

Return the preferred cursor column of the current widget, or None if it has none.

Raises:

TypeError – the current widget has no get_pref_col method.

keypress(size: tuple[int, int], key: str) → str | None¶

Rebuild the pop-up overlay chain for size and forward the keypress to it.

A key the topmost pop-up leaves unhandled goes to the on_unhandled_key callback its launcher set, if any; see CompositeCanvas.set_pop_up.

mouse_event(size: tuple[int, int], event: str, button: int, col: int, row: int, focus: bool) → bool | None¶

Rebuild the pop-up overlay chain for size and forward the mouse event to it.

move_cursor_to_coords(size: tuple[int, int], x: int, y: int) → bool¶

Move the cursor of the current widget to (x, y).

Raises:

TypeError – the current widget has no move_cursor_to_coords method.

pack(size: tuple[int, int] | tuple[()] = (), focus: bool = False) → tuple[int, int]¶

Rebuild the pop-up overlay chain for size and return the current widget’s packed size.

render(size: tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → Canvas¶

Rebuild the pop-up overlay chain for size and render the resulting widget.

Special Widget Classes¶

WidgetDisable¶

class urwid.WidgetDisable(original_widget: WrappedWidget, *, disabled: bool = True)¶

Decoration widget that disables interaction with the widget it wraps.

While disabled is True, this widget is never selectable, reports no cursor, and always passes focus=False to the wrapped widget, even if it somehow does become the focus. While it is False, focus, input and the cursor pass through to the wrapped widget unchanged. The look of a disabled widget is left to the application, for example an AttrMap around it.

Parameters:

  • original_widget – the widget being disabled

  • disabled – start disabled; False starts with the wrapped widget enabled

>>> from urwid import Button
>>> w = WidgetDisable(Button("Ok"))
>>> w.selectable()
False
>>> w.disabled = False
>>> w.selectable()
True

Wrap original_widget, disabled unless disabled is False.

property disabled: bool¶

Whether interaction with the wrapped widget is disabled; setting it redraws the widget.

enter_selectable(*, reverse: bool = False) → None¶

Forward the entry hook to original_widget unless disabled: a disabled widget is never entered.

property get_cursor_coords: Callable[[tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int]], tuple[int, int] | None]¶

Return the wrapped widget’s get_cursor_coords method while enabled, if it has one.

property get_pref_col: Callable[[tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int]], int | None]¶

Return the wrapped widget’s get_pref_col method while enabled, if it has one.

keypress(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], key: str) → str | None¶

Return key unhandled while disabled, otherwise pass it to the wrapped widget.

mouse_event(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], event: str, button: int, col: int, row: int, focus: bool) → bool | None¶

Leave the event unhandled while disabled, otherwise pass it to the wrapped widget.

property move_cursor_to_coords: Callable[[tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], int, int], bool]¶

Return the wrapped widget’s move_cursor_to_coords method while enabled, if it has one.

pack(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → tuple[int, int]¶

Return the size required by the wrapped widget, passing focus=False while disabled.

render(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → CompositeCanvas¶

Render the wrapped widget into a canvas, passing focus=False while disabled.

rows(size: tuple[int], focus: bool = False) → int¶

Return the number of rows the wrapped widget occupies, passing focus=False while disabled.

selectable() → bool¶

Return False while disabled, otherwise whether the wrapped widget can take the input focus.

sizing() → frozenset[Sizing]¶

Return the set of sizing modes supported by the wrapped widget.

WidgetPlaceholder¶

class urwid.WidgetPlaceholder(original_widget: WrappedWidget)¶

Do-nothing decoration widget that can be used for swapping between widgets.

Swaps happen without modifying the container of this widget.

This can be useful for making an interface with a number of distinct pages or for showing and hiding menu or status bars.

The widget displayed is stored as the self.original_widget property and can be changed by assigning a new widget to it.

Wrap original_widget, warning when it does not implement the Widget API.

Deprecated since version 2.4.0: Wrapping an object that does not implement the Widget API (see AbstractWidget) is deprecated. Support will be removed in version 7.0.

Container Widget Classes¶

Frame¶

class urwid.Frame(body: BodyWidget, header: HeaderWidget | None = None, footer: FooterWidget | None = None, focus_part: Literal['header', 'footer', 'body'] | AbstractWidget = 'body', *, select_navigation: bool = False)¶

Frame widget is a box widget with optional header and footer flow widgets placed above and below it.

Note

The main difference between a Frame and a Pile widget defined as: Pile([(‘pack’, header), body, (‘pack’, footer)]) is that the Frame will not automatically change focus up and down in response to keystrokes.

Initialize a new Frame instance.

Parameters:

  • body – a box widget for the body of the frame

  • header – a flow widget for above the body (or None)

  • footer – a flow widget for below the body (or None)

  • focus_part – ‘header’, ‘footer’ or ‘body’

  • select_navigation – handle the 'next selectable' and 'prev selectable' commands, see Moving the Focus with Tab.

Raises:

ValueError – focus_part is not one of the three frame parts.

Deprecated since version 2.4.0: Passing a header, body or footer that does not implement the Widget API is deprecated. Support will be removed in version 7.0.

property body: BodyWidget¶

Return the body widget.

property contents: MutableMapping[Literal['header', 'footer', 'body'], tuple[BodyWidget | HeaderWidget | FooterWidget, None]]¶

Return a dict-like object similar to the following.

{
    "body": (body_widget, None),
    "header": (header_widget, None),  # if frame has a header
    "footer": (footer_widget, None),  # if frame has a footer
}

This object may be used to read or update the contents of the Frame.

The values are similar to the list-like .contents objects used in other containers with (Widget, options) tuples, but are constrained to keys for each of the three usual parts of a Frame. When other keys are used a KeyError will be raised.

Currently, all options are None, but using the options() method to create the options value is recommended for forwards compatibility.

property focus: BodyWidget | HeaderWidget | FooterWidget¶

Return the child Widget in focus: the body, header or footer widget. Read-only.

property focus_position: Literal['header', 'footer', 'body']¶

Return which part of the frame is in focus: ‘body’, ‘header’ or ‘footer’.

Returns:

one of ‘header’, ‘footer’ or ‘body’.

property footer: FooterWidget | None¶

Return the footer widget, or None if there is no footer.

frame_top_bottom(size: tuple[int, int], focus: bool) → tuple[tuple[int, int], tuple[int, int]]¶

Calculate the number of rows for the header and footer.

Parameters:

  • size – See Widget.render() for details

  • focus – True if this widget is in focus

Returns:

(head rows, foot rows),(orig head, orig foot) orig head/foot are from rows() calls.

Return the cursor coordinates of the focus widget.

property header: HeaderWidget | None¶

Return the header widget, or None if there is no header.

Pass keypress to widget in focus.

Pass mouse event to appropriate part of frame. Focus may be changed on button 1 press.

Return None as a placeholder for future options.

Vertically stacked list of widgets.

Create the ListBox widget.

The widgets are to be displayed inside the list box.

calculate_visible(size: tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → VisibleInfo | tuple[None, None, None]¶

Return the widgets that would be displayed in the ListBox given the current size and focus.

see Widget.render() for parameter details

Returns:

(middle, top, bottom) or (None, None, None)

middle

(row offset*(when +ve) or *inset*(when -ve), *focus widget, focus position, focus rows, cursor coords or None)

top

(# lines to trim off top, list of (widget, position, rows) tuples above focus in order from bottom to top)

bottom

(# lines to trim off bottom, list of (widget, position, rows) tuples below focus in order from top to bottom)

change_focus(size: tuple[int, int], position: _K, offset_inset: int = 0, coming_from: Literal['above', 'below'] | None = None, cursor_coords: tuple[int | str, int] | tuple[int | str] | None = None, snap_rows: int | None = None) → None¶

Change the current focus widget.

This is used internally by methods that know the widget’s size.

See also set_focus().

Parameters:

  • size – see Widget.render() for details

  • position – a position compatible with self._body.set_focus()

  • offset_inset – either the number of rows between the top of the listbox and the start of the focus widget (+ve value) or the number of lines of the focus widget hidden off the top edge of the listbox (-ve value) or 0 if the top edge of the focus widget is aligned with the top edge of the listbox (default if unspecified)

  • coming_from – either ‘above’, ‘below’ or unspecified None

  • cursor_coords – (x, y) tuple indicating the desired column and row for the cursor, a (x,) tuple indicating only the column for the cursor, or unspecified

  • snap_rows – the maximum number of extra rows to scroll when trying to “snap” a selectable focus into the view

Raises:

  • TypeError – the body does not implement set_focus.

  • ListBoxError – offset_inset leaves no row of the target visible, or cursor_coords names a row outside the target widget.

  • ValueError – the cursor row is unspecified and coming_from is neither 'above' nor 'below'.

property contents: ListBoxContentsProto[_K]¶

An object that allows reading widgets from the ListBox’s list walker.

Widgets are read as a (widget, options) tuple. None is currently the only value for options.

Warning

This object may not be used to set or iterate over contents.

You must use the list walker stored as body to perform manipulation and iteration, if supported.

ends_visible(size: tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → list[Literal['top', 'bottom']]¶

Return a list that may contain 'top' and/or 'bottom'.

i.e. this function will return one of: [], ['top'], ['bottom'] or ['top', 'bottom'].

convenience function for checking whether the top and bottom of the list are visible

property focus: AbstractFlowWidget | None¶

The child widget in focus or None when ListBox is empty.

Return the widget in focus according to our list walker.

focus_next_match(predicate: Callable[[AbstractFlowWidget], bool], *, reverse: bool = False, wrap: bool = True) → _K | None¶

Move the focus to the next widget for which predicate returns true.

The body is walked lazily from the position next to the focus in the search direction, so a match before the end of the body is found without reading the rest of it. A wrapped search reads the other side of the focus whole, and checks the widget in focus last, so a single match is found again.

>>> import urwid
>>> listbox = urwid.ListBox([urwid.Text(word) for word in ("apple", "pear", "plum", "peach")])
>>> listbox.focus_next_match(lambda widget: widget.text.startswith("p"))
1
>>> listbox.focus_next_match(lambda widget: widget.text.startswith("p"), reverse=True)
3
>>> listbox.focus_next_match(lambda widget: widget.text == "apple", wrap=False) is None
True
>>> listbox.focus_position
3
Parameters:

  • predicate – called with each candidate widget.

  • reverse – search towards the top of the body.

  • wrap – continue from the other end of the body once this end is reached. Only a body that ends, or declares wrap_around, has an end to stop at; one that cycles without declaring it is searched once round from the focus either way.

Returns:

the new focus position, or None when nothing matches and the focus stays where it was.

property focus_position: _K¶

Return the position of the child widget in focus.

The valid values for this position depend on the list walker in use.

Raises:

IndexError – the ListBox is empty.

See Widget.get_cursor_coords() for details.

get_first_visible_pos(size: tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → int¶

Return the index of the first visible item.

get_focus_offset_inset(size: tuple[int, int]) → tuple[int, int]¶

Return (offset rows, inset rows) for focus widget.

ListBoxError – the stored inset fraction is invalid or exceeds the rows of the focus widget.

get_scrollpos(size: tuple[int, int] | None = None, focus: bool = False) → int¶

Return the current scrolling position.

get_visible_amount(size: tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → int¶

Return the number of items currently visible.

keypress(size: tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], key: str) → str | None¶

Move selection through the list elements scrolling when necessary.

Keystrokes are first passed to widget in focus in case that widget can handle them.

Keystrokes handled by this widget are:

up

up one line (or widget)

down

down one line (or widget)

page up

move cursor up one listbox length (or widget)

page down

move cursor down one listbox length (or widget)

With select_navigation, unhandled 'next selectable' and 'prev selectable' commands move the focus to the next or previous selectable widget.

make_cursor_visible(size: tuple[int, int]) → None¶

Shift the focus widget so that its cursor is visible.

Pass the event to the contained widgets.

May change focus on button 1 press.

Deprecated since version 2.4.0: Support for a contained widget that does not implement mouse_event is deprecated. Support will be removed in version 7.0.

options() → None¶

There are currently no options for ListBox contents.

Return None as a placeholder for future options.

render(size: tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → CompositeCanvas | SolidCanvas¶

Render ListBox and return canvas.

see Widget.render() for details

A flow size renders every widget of the body, with the rows rows() reports.

Raises:

ListBoxError – the rendered contents do not fit the reported rows, a child widget renders a different number of rows or cursor coordinates than it calculated, or the list walker returns a next position pointing at itself.

require_relative_scroll(size: tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → bool¶

Widget require relative scroll due to performance limitations of real lines count calculation.

rows(size: tuple[int], focus: bool = False) → int¶

Return the rows of all widgets in the body at the width in size.

The focus widget is measured in focus and the others out of focus, as a render measures them, whatever focus is. A child whose row count depends on its focus breaks the box layout as well, which a render reports as a ListBoxError.

>>> from urwid import Text
>>> ListBox([Text("one two"), Text("three")]).rows((5,))
3
Raises:

ListBoxError – the body does not support the scrolling protocol, or it wraps around.

rows_max(size: tuple[int, int] | None = None, focus: bool = False) → int¶

Scrollable protocol for sized iterable and not wrapped around contents.

scroll_to_bottom() → None¶

Move the focus to the last position of the body and show it at the bottom, as end does.

The last position gets the focus whether its widget is selectable or not, unlike focus_last_selectable(). An empty body is left as it is.

Raises:

TypeError – the body does not implement positions.

scroll_to_top() → None¶

Move the focus to the first position of the body and show it at the top, as home does.

The first position gets the focus whether its widget is selectable or not, unlike focus_first_selectable(). An empty body is left as it is.

Raises:

TypeError – the body does not implement positions.

selectable() → bool¶

Return whether the ListBox accepts the input focus.

With focus_when_empty False it does not while its body is empty.

set_focus(position: _K, coming_from: Literal['above', 'below'] | None = None) → None¶

Set the focus position and try to keep the old focus in view.

Without coming_from, preserve the target widget’s cursor and nested focus. With coming_from, move its cursor from the indicated edge.

Parameters:

  • position – a position compatible with self._body.set_focus()

  • coming_from – set to ‘above’ or ‘below’ if you know that old position is above or below the new position.

Raises:

  • ListBoxError – coming_from is not 'above', 'below' or None.

  • TypeError – the body does not implement set_focus.

  • IndexError – the ListBox is empty.

set_focus_valign(valign: Literal['top', 'middle', 'bottom'] | VAlign | tuple[Literal['relative', WHSettings.RELATIVE], int]) → None¶

Set the focus widget’s display offset and inset.

Parameters:

valign – one of: ‘top’, ‘middle’, ‘bottom’ (‘relative’, percentage 0=top 100=bottom)

shift_focus(size: tuple[int, int], offset_inset: int) → None¶

Move the location of the current focus relative to the top.

This is used internally by methods that know the widget’s size.

See also set_focus_valign().

Parameters:

  • size – see Widget.render() for details

  • offset_inset – either the number of rows between the top of the listbox and the start of the focus widget (+ve value) or the number of lines of the focus widget hidden off the top edge of the listbox (-ve value) or 0 if the top edge of the focus widget is aligned with the top edge of the listbox.

Raises:

ListBoxError – offset_inset falls outside the listbox rows or the rows of the focus widget.

Update self.pref_col from the focus widget.

Columns¶

class urwid.Columns(widget_list: Iterable[AbstractBoxWidget | AbstractFlowWidget | tuple[Literal['pack', WHSettings.PACK], AbstractFlowWidget | AbstractFixedWidget] | tuple[int, AbstractBoxWidget | AbstractFlowWidget] | tuple[Literal['given', WHSettings.GIVEN], int, AbstractBoxWidget | AbstractFlowWidget] | tuple[Literal['weight', WHSettings.WEIGHT], int | float, AbstractBoxWidget | AbstractFlowWidget]], dividechars: int = 0, focus_column: int | AbstractWidget | None = None, min_width: int = 1, box_columns: Iterable[int] | None = None, *, select_navigation: bool = False)¶

Widgets arranged horizontally in columns from left to right.

Sends "focus changed" after focus_position changed, also through a change of contents. Its handlers receive the container, the old and the new focus position, which is None while it is empty.

Initialize a new Columns instance.

Parameters:

  • widget_list – iterable of flow or box widgets

  • dividechars – number of blank characters between columns

  • focus_column – index into widget_list of column in focus or focused widget instance, if None the first selectable widget will be chosen.

  • min_width – minimum width for each column which is not calling widget.pack() in widget_list.

  • box_columns – a list of column indexes containing box widgets whose height is set to the maximum of the rows required by columns not listed in box_columns.

  • select_navigation – handle the 'next selectable' and 'prev selectable' commands, see Moving the Focus with Tab.

Raises:

  • ColumnsError – an item of widget_list is not a widget or a valid (width, widget) pair.

  • ValueError – focus_column is a widget that is not in widget_list.

Warns ColumnsWarning:

an item of widget_list is not a widget. A 'pack' column is listed in box_columns.

widget_list may also contain tuples such as:

(given_width, widget)

make this column given_width screen columns wide, where given_width is an int

('given', given_width, widget)

the same as (given_width, widget), in the expanded form that repeats the contents options. 'fixed' is accepted as an older name for 'given'.

('pack', widget)

call pack() to calculate the width of this column

('weight', weight, widget)

give this column a relative weight (number) to calculate its width from th screen columns remaining

Widgets not in a tuple are the same as ('weight', 1, widget)

If the Columns widget is treated as a box widget then all children are treated as box widgets, and box_columns is ignored.

If the Columns widget is treated as a flow widget then the rows are calculated as the largest rows() returned from all columns except the ones listed in box_columns. The box widgets in box_columns will be displayed with this calculated number of rows, filling the full height.

column_widths(size: tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → list[int]¶

Return a list of column widths.

0 values in the list means hide the corresponding column completely

static options(width_type: Literal['pack', WHSettings.PACK], width_amount: int | float | None = 1, box_widget: bool = False) → tuple[Literal[WHSettings.PACK], None, bool]¶
static options(width_type: Literal['given', WHSettings.GIVEN], width_amount: int = 1, box_widget: bool = False) → tuple[Literal[WHSettings.GIVEN], int, bool]
static options(width_type: Literal['weight', WHSettings.WEIGHT] = WHSettings.WEIGHT, width_amount: int | float = 1, box_widget: bool = False) → tuple[Literal[WHSettings.WEIGHT], int | float, bool]
static options(width_type: Literal['pack', 'given', 'weight', WHSettings.PACK, WHSettings.GIVEN, WHSettings.WEIGHT] = WHSettings.WEIGHT, width_amount: int | float | None = 1, box_widget: bool = False) → tuple[Literal[WHSettings.PACK], None, bool] | tuple[Literal[WHSettings.GIVEN], int, bool] | tuple[Literal[WHSettings.WEIGHT], int | float, bool]

Return a new options tuple for use in a Columns .contents list.

This sets an entry’s width type: one of the following:

'pack'

Call the widget’s Widget.pack() method to determine how wide this column should be. width_amount is ignored.

'given'

Make column exactly width_amount screen-columns wide.

'weight'

Allocate the remaining space to this column by using width_amount as a weight value.

Parameters:

  • width_type – 'pack', 'given' or 'weight'

  • width_amount – None for 'pack', a number of screen columns for 'given' or a weight value (number) for 'weight'

  • box_widget – set to True if this widget is to be treated as a box widget when the Columns widget itself is treated as a flow widget.

Raises:

ColumnsError – width_type and width_amount are not a valid combination.

Get packed size for widget.

Raises:

ColumnsError – size is () and the children cannot be sized as a fixed widget.

render(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → SolidCanvas | CompositeCanvas¶

Render columns and return canvas.

Parameters:

  • size – see Widget.render() for details

  • focus – True if this widget is in focus

Raises:

ColumnsError – the Columns has no visible column to render, or size is () and the children cannot be sized as a fixed widget.

rows(size: tuple[int], focus: bool = False) → int¶

Return the number of rows required by the columns.

This only makes sense if contents contains flow widgets.

see Widget.rows() for details

selectable() → bool¶

Return whether any child widget is selectable.

Asked on every call rather than cached, since a child such as WidgetPlaceholder may change its selectability after it was added.

sizing() → frozenset[Sizing]¶

Sizing supported by widget.

Returns:

Calculated widget sizing

Warns ColumnsWarning:

a column’s width type does not suit its widget’s sizing, or no sizing fits all columns and the BOX/FLOW fallback is used.

Due to the nature of container with mutable contents, this method cannot be cached.

Rules: * WEIGHT BOX -> BOX * GIVEN BOX -> Can be included in FIXED and FLOW depends on the other columns * PACK BOX -> Unsupported * BOX-only widget without box_columns disallow FLOW render

  • WEIGHT FLOW -> FLOW

  • GIVEN FLOW -> FIXED (known width and widget knows its height) + FLOW (historic)

  • PACK FLOW -> FLOW (widget fit in provided size)

  • WEIGHT FIXED -> Need also FLOW or/and BOX to properly render due to width calculation

  • GIVEN FIXED -> Unsupported

  • PACK FIXED -> FIXED (widget knows its size)

Backward compatibility rules: * GIVEN BOX -> Allow BOX

BOX can be only if ALL widgets support BOX. FIXED can be only if no BOX without “box_columns” flag and no strict FLOW.

>>> from urwid import BigText, Edit, SolidFill, Text, Thin3x3Font
>>> font = Thin3x3Font()

# BOX-only widget >>> Columns((SolidFill(“#”),)) <Columns box widget (1 item)>

# BOX-only widget with “get height from max” >>> Columns((SolidFill(“#”),), box_columns=(0,)) <Columns box widget (1 item)>

# FLOW-only >>> Columns((Edit(),)) <Columns selectable flow widget (1 item)>

# FLOW allowed by “box_columns” >>> Columns((Edit(), SolidFill(“#”)), box_columns=(1,)) <Columns selectable flow widget (2 items) focus_column=0>

# FLOW/FIXED >>> Columns((Text(“T”),)) <Columns fixed/flow widget (1 item)>

# GIVEN BOX only -> BOX only >>> Columns(((5, SolidFill(“#”)),), box_columns=(0,)) <Columns box widget (1 item)>

# No FLOW - BOX only >>> Columns(((5, SolidFill(“#”)), SolidFill(“*”)), box_columns=(0, 1)) <Columns box widget (2 items) focus_column=0>

# FIXED only -> FIXED (and FLOW via drop/expand) >>> Columns(((WHSettings.PACK, BigText(“1”, font)),)) <Columns fixed/flow widget (1 item)>

# Invalid sizing combination -> use fallback settings (and produce warning) >>> Columns(((WHSettings.PACK, SolidFill(“#”)),)) <Columns box/flow widget (1 item)>

# Special case: empty columns widget sizing is impossible to calculate >>> Columns(()) <Columns box/flow widget ()>

Pile¶

class urwid.Pile(widget_list: Iterable[AbstractWidget | tuple[Literal['pack', WHSettings.PACK], AbstractFlowWidget | AbstractFixedWidget] | tuple[int, AbstractBoxWidget] | tuple[Literal['given', WHSettings.GIVEN], int, AbstractBoxWidget] | tuple[Literal['weight', WHSettings.WEIGHT], int | float, AbstractBoxWidget | AbstractFlowWidget]], focus_item: AbstractWidget | int | None = None, *, select_navigation: bool = False)¶

A pile of widgets stacked vertically from top to bottom.

Sends "focus changed" after focus_position changed, also through a change of contents. Its handlers receive the container, the old and the new focus position, which is None while it is empty.

Build the pile from a list of child widgets.

Parameters:

  • widget_list – child widgets

  • focus_item – child widget that gets the focus initially. Chooses the first selectable widget if unset.

  • select_navigation – handle the 'next selectable' and 'prev selectable' commands, see Moving the Focus with Tab.

Raises:

PileError – an item of widget_list is not a widget or a valid (height, widget) pair.

Warns PileWarning:

an item of widget_list is not a widget.

widget_list may also contain tuples such as:

(given_height, widget)

always treat widget as a box widget and give it given_height rows, where given_height is an int

('given', given_height, widget)

the same as (given_height, widget), in the expanded form that repeats the contents options. 'fixed' is accepted as an older name for 'given'.

('pack', widget)

allow widget to calculate its own height by calling its rows() method, i.e. treat it as a flow widget.

('weight', weight, widget)

if the pile is treated as a box widget then treat widget as a box widget with a height based on its relative weight value, otherwise treat the same as ('pack', widget).

Widgets not in a tuple are the same as ('weight', 1, widget)`

Note

If the Pile is treated as a box widget there must be at least one 'weight' tuple in widget_list.

property contents: MonitoredFocusList[tuple[AbstractFlowWidget | AbstractFixedWidget, tuple[Literal[WHSettings.PACK], None]] | tuple[AbstractBoxWidget, tuple[Literal[WHSettings.GIVEN], int]] | tuple[AbstractBoxWidget | AbstractFlowWidget, tuple[Literal[WHSettings.WEIGHT], int | float]]]¶

The contents of this Pile as a list of (widget, options) tuples.

options currently may be one of

('pack', None)

allow widget to calculate its own height by calling its rows method, i.e. treat it as a flow widget.

('given', n)

Always treat widget as a box widget with a given height of n rows.

('weight', w)

If the Pile itself is treated as a box widget then the value w will be used as a relative weight for assigning rows to this box widget. If the Pile is being treated as a flow widget then this is the same as ('pack', None) and the w value is ignored.

If the Pile itself is treated as a box widget then at least one widget must have a ('weight', w) options value, or the Pile will not be able to grow to fill the required number of rows.

This list may be modified like a normal list and the Pile widget will updated automatically.

See also

Create new options tuples with the options() method

The child widget in focus or None when Pile is empty.

sizing() → frozenset[Sizing]¶

Sizing supported by widget.

Returns:

Calculated widget sizing

Warns PileWarning:

an item’s height type does not suit its widget’s sizing.

Due to the nature of container with mutable contents, this method cannot be cached.

Rules: * WEIGHT BOX -> BOX * GIVEN BOX -> FLOW (height is known) & BOX (can be shrinked/padded) * PACK BOX -> Unsupported

  • WEIGHT FLOW -> FLOW

  • GIVEN FLOW -> Unsupported

  • PACK FLOW -> FLOW

  • WEIGHT FIXED -> Need also FLOW or/and BOX to properly render due to width calculation

  • GIVEN FIXED -> Unsupported

  • PACK FIXED -> FIXED (widget knows its size)

>>> from urwid import BigText, ProgressBar, SolidFill, Text, Thin3x3Font
>>> font = Thin3x3Font()

# BOX-only widget >>> Pile((SolidFill(“#”),)) <Pile box widget (1 item)>

# GIVEN BOX -> BOX/FLOW >>> Pile(((10, SolidFill(“#”)),)) <Pile box/flow widget (1 item)>

# FLOW-only >>> Pile((ProgressBar(None, None),)) <Pile flow widget (1 item)>

# FIXED -> FIXED >>> Pile(((WHSettings.PACK, BigText(“0”, font)),)) <Pile fixed widget (1 item)>

# FLOW/FIXED -> FLOW/FIXED >>> Pile(((WHSettings.PACK, Text(“text”)),)) <Pile fixed/flow widget (1 item)>

# FLOW + FIXED widgets -> FLOW/FIXED >>> Pile((ProgressBar(None, None), (WHSettings.PACK, BigText(“0”, font)))) <Pile fixed/flow widget (2 items) focus_item=0>

# GIVEN BOX + FIXED widgets -> BOX/FLOW/FIXED (GIVEN BOX allows overriding its height & allows any width) >>> Pile(((10, SolidFill(“#”)), (WHSettings.PACK, BigText(“0”, font)))) <Pile widget (2 items) focus_item=0>

# Invalid sizing combination -> use fallback settings (and produce warning) >>> Pile(((WHSettings.WEIGHT, 1, BigText(“0”, font)),)) <Pile box/flow widget (1 item)>

# Special case: empty pile widget sizing is impossible to calculate >>> Pile(()) <Pile box/flow widget ()>

GridFlow¶

class urwid.GridFlow(cells: Iterable[AbstractFlowWidget], cell_width: int, h_sep: int, v_sep: int, align: Literal['left', 'center', 'right'] | Align | tuple[Literal['relative', WHSettings.RELATIVE], int], focus: int | AbstractFlowWidget | None = None, *, select_navigation: bool = False)¶

Flow widget that renders all the widgets it contains the same width.

Arranges them from left to right and top to bottom.

Sends "focus changed" after focus_position changed, also through a change of contents. Its handlers receive the container, the old and the new focus position, which is None while it is empty.

Create the GridFlow widget.

Parameters:

  • cells – iterable of flow widgets to display

  • cell_width – column width for each cell

  • h_sep – blank columns between each cell horizontally

  • v_sep – blank rows between cells vertically (if more than one row is required to display all the cells)

  • align – horizontal alignment of cells, one of: ‘left’, ‘center’, ‘right’, (‘relative’, percentage 0=left 100=right)

  • focus – widget index or widget instance to focus on

  • select_navigation – handle the 'next selectable' and 'prev selectable' commands over the cells in their contents order, see Moving the Focus with Tab.

property base_widget: GridFlow¶

Return self: GridFlow is a container, not a decoration.

property cell_width: int¶

The width of each cell in the GridFlow.

Setting this value affects all cells.

property contents: MonitoredFocusList[tuple[AbstractFlowWidget, tuple[Literal[WHSettings.GIVEN], int]]]¶

The contents of this GridFlow as a list of (widget, options) tuples.

options is currently a tuple in the form (‘given’, number). number is the number of screen columns to allocate to this cell. ‘given’ is the only type accepted at this time.

This list may be modified like a normal list and the GridFlow widget will update automatically.

See also

Create new options tuples with the options() method.

enter_selectable(*, reverse: bool = False) → None¶

Start at the first selectable cell, or at the last one when reverse is set.

It is the entry hook a parent container calls, and acts only when select_navigation is set, see Moving the Focus with Tab.

Parameters:

reverse – start at the last selectable cell instead of the first one.

property focus: AbstractFlowWidget | None¶

The child widget in focus or None when GridFlow is empty.

property focus_position: int¶

Index of child widget in focus.

Raises IndexError if read when GridFlow is empty, or when set to an invalid index.

Raises:

IndexError – the GridFlow is empty.

Arrange the cells into columns (and possibly a pile) for display, input or to calculate rows.

Also updates the display widget.

get_pref_col(size: tuple[int] | tuple[()]) → int | None¶

Return pref col from display widget, or None if the widget in focus has no preferred column.

keypress(size: tuple[int] | tuple[()], key: str) → str | None¶

Pass keypress to display widget for handling.

Captures focus changes. With select_navigation, unhandled 'next selectable' and 'prev selectable' commands move the focus to the next or previous selectable cell.

mouse_event(size: tuple[int] | tuple[()], event: str, button: int, col: int, row: int, focus: bool) → bool | None¶

Handle a mouse event, updating the focus based on the resulting display widget.

Returns:

True when a cell handled the event or the focus moved to another cell, otherwise the result of the display widget, so an event such as the mouse wheel stays unhandled for a parent like ListBox.

Overlay¶

class urwid.Overlay(top_w: TopWidget, bottom_w: BottomWidget, align: Literal['left', 'center', 'right'] | Align | tuple[Literal['relative', 'fixed left', 'fixed right', WHSettings.RELATIVE], int], width: Literal['pack', WHSettings.PACK] | int | tuple[Literal['relative', WHSettings.RELATIVE], int] | None, valign: Literal['top', 'middle', 'bottom'] | VAlign | tuple[Literal['relative', 'fixed top', 'fixed bottom', WHSettings.RELATIVE], int], height: Literal['pack', WHSettings.PACK] | int | tuple[Literal['relative', WHSettings.RELATIVE], int] | None, min_width: int | None = None, min_height: int | None = None, left: int = 0, right: int = 0, top: int = 0, bottom: int = 0)¶

Overlay contains two widgets and renders one on top of the other.

Top widget can be Box, Flow or Fixed. Bottom widget should be Box.

Build the widget overlaying top_w on bottom_w.

Parameters:

  • top_w – a flow, box or fixed widget to overlay “on top”.

  • bottom_w – a box widget to appear “below” previous widget.

  • align – alignment, one of 'left', 'center', 'right' or ('relative', percentage 0=left 100=right)

  • width –

    width type, one of:

    'pack'

    if top_w is a fixed widget

    given width

    integer number of columns wide

    ('relative', percentage of total width)

    make top_w width related to container width

  • valign – alignment mode, one of 'top', 'middle', 'bottom' or ('relative', percentage 0=top 100=bottom)

  • height –

    one of:

    'pack'

    if top_w is a flow or fixed widget

    given height

    integer number of rows high

    ('relative', percentage of total height)

    make top_w height related to container height

  • min_width – the minimum number of columns for top_w when width is not fixed.

  • min_height – minimum number of rows for top_w when height is not fixed.

  • left – a fixed number of columns to add on the left.

  • right – a fixed number of columns to add on the right.

  • top – a fixed number of rows to add on the top.

  • bottom – a fixed number of rows to add on the bottom.

Overlay widgets behave similarly to Padding and Filler widgets when determining the size and position of top_w. bottom_w is always rendered the full size available “below” top_w.

Deprecated since version 2.4.0: Passing a top_w or bottom_w that does not implement the Widget API is deprecated. Support will be removed in version 7.0.

property align: Align | tuple[Literal[WHSettings.RELATIVE], int]¶

Return the simplified horizontal alignment of the top widget.

property bottom_w: BottomWidget¶

Widget appearing “below” top_w.

calculate_padding_filler(size: tuple[int, int], focus: bool) → tuple[int, int, int, int]¶

Return (padding left, right, filler top, bottom).

Raises:

OverlayError – the top widget is FIXED but reports no height.

property contents: MutableSequence[tuple[TopWidget | BottomWidget, OverlayOptions]]¶

A list-like object holding the overlay’s widgets and their options.

It is similar to:

[(bottom_w, bottom_options)),
 (top_w, top_options)]

This object may be used to read or update top and bottom widgets and top widgets’s options, but no widgets may be added or removed.

top_options takes the form (align_type, align_amount, width_type, width_amount, min_width, left, right, valign_type, valign_amount, height_type, height_amount, min_height, top, bottom)

bottom_options is always (‘left’, None, ‘relative’, 100, None, 0, 0, ‘top’, None, ‘relative’, 100, None, 0, 0) which means that bottom widget always covers the full area of the Overlay. writing a different value for bottom_options raises an OverlayError.

property focus: TopWidget¶

Return the top widget, which always has the focus.

property focus_position: Literal[1]¶

Return the top widget position (currently always 1).

get_cursor_coords(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int]) → tuple[int, int] | None¶

Return cursor coords from top_w, if any.

property height: int | Literal[WHSettings.FLOW, WHSettings.PACK] | tuple[Literal[WHSettings.RELATIVE], int] | tuple[Literal[WHSettings.WEIGHT], int | float]¶

Return the simplified height of the top widget.

keypress(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], key: str) → str | None¶

Pass keypress to top_w.

mouse_event(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], event: str, button: int, col: int, row: int, focus: bool) → bool | None¶

Pass event to top_w, ignore if outside of top_w.

static options(align_type: Literal['left', 'center', 'right', 'relative', WHSettings.RELATIVE] | Align, align_amount: int | None, width_type: Literal['clip', 'pack', 'relative', 'given'] | WHSettings, width_amount: int | None, valign_type: Literal['top', 'middle', 'bottom', 'relative', WHSettings.RELATIVE] | VAlign, valign_amount: int | None, height_type: Literal['flow', 'pack', 'relative', 'given'] | WHSettings, height_amount: int | None, min_width: int | None = None, min_height: int | None = None, left: int = 0, right: int = 0, top: int = 0, bottom: int = 0) → OverlayOptions¶

Return a new options tuple for use in this Overlay’s .contents mapping.

This is the common container API to create options for replacing the top widget of this Overlay. It is provided for completeness but is not necessarily the easiest way to change the overlay parameters. See also set_overlay_parameters()

Raises:

ValueError – align or valign names an unknown alignment type.

Return the size the widget would render as, for FIXED sizing.

Raises:

OverlayError – a FIXED render is requested but the overlay parameters do not resolve to a fixed size.

set_overlay_parameters(align: Literal['left', 'center', 'right'] | Align | tuple[Literal['relative', 'fixed left', 'fixed right', WHSettings.RELATIVE], int], width: Literal['pack', WHSettings.PACK] | int | tuple[Literal['relative', 'fixed left', 'fixed right', WHSettings.RELATIVE], int] | None, valign: Literal['top', 'middle', 'bottom'] | VAlign | tuple[Literal['relative', 'fixed top', 'fixed bottom', WHSettings.RELATIVE], int], height: Literal['pack', WHSettings.PACK] | int | tuple[Literal['relative', 'fixed top', 'fixed bottom', WHSettings.RELATIVE], int] | None, min_width: int | None = None, min_height: int | None = None, left: int = 0, right: int = 0, top: int = 0, bottom: int = 0) → None¶

Adjust the overlay size and position parameters.

See __init__() for a description of the parameters.

Raises:

OverlayError – valign is not a vertical alignment value.

sizing() → frozenset[Sizing]¶

Actual widget sizing.

Returns:

Sizing information depends on the top widget sizing and sizing parameters.

Rules: * BOX sizing is always supported provided by the bottom widget * FLOW sizing is supported if top widget has: * * PACK height type and FLOW supported by the TOP widget * * BOX supported by TOP widget AND height amount AND height type GIVEN of min_height * FIXED sizing is supported if top widget has: * * PACK width type and FIXED supported by the TOP widget * * width amount and GIVEN width or min_width AND: * * * FLOW supported by the TOP widget AND PACK height type * * * BOX supported by the TOP widget AND height_amount and GIVEN height or min height

Warns OverlayWarning:

the top widget does not support the sizing its width or height type needs.

property top_w: TopWidget¶

Widget overlaid “on top” of bottom_w.

Return the size to pass to top_w.

Return the simplified vertical alignment of the top widget.

BarGraph¶

class urwid.BarGraph(attlist: Sequence[str | tuple[str, str]], hatt: list[str] | None = None, satt: Mapping[tuple[int, int], str] | None = None)¶

Box widget that renders a bar graph from a sequence of data values.

Deprecated since version 4.0.10: Overriding get_data() in a subclass, or assigning get_data on an instance, is supported for backwards compatibility only. Call set_data() instead, so that the rendered canvas can be cached. This API will be removed in version 7.0.

Create a bar graph with the passed display characteristics.

See set_segment_attributes() for a description of the parameters.

calculate_bar_widths(size: tuple[int, int], bardata: Sequence[Sequence[float | int]]) → list[int]¶

Return a list of bar widths, one for each bar in data.

If self.bar_width is None this implementation will stretch the bars across the available space specified by maxcol.

calculate_display(size: tuple[int, int]) → list[tuple[int, list[tuple[int | tuple[int, int] | tuple[int, int, int], int]]]]¶

Calculate display data.

hlines_display(disp: list[tuple[int, list[tuple[int | tuple[int, int] | tuple[int, int, int], int]]]], top: float, hlines: Sequence[float | int], maxrow: int) → list[tuple[int, list[tuple[int | tuple[int, int] | tuple[int, int, int], int]]]]¶

Add hlines to display structure represented as bar_type tuple values.

The tuple is (bg, 0-5) where bg is the segment that has the hline on it, and 0-5 is the hline graphic to use where 0 is a regular underscore and 1-5 are the UTF-8 horizontal scan line characters.

render(size: tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → CompositeCanvas¶

Render BarGraph.

Raises:

BarGraphError – a graph character does not render as a single row.

selectable() → Literal[False]¶

Return False.

set_bar_width(width: int | None) → None¶

Set a preferred bar width for calculate_bar_widths to use.

Parameters:

width – width of bar or None for automatic width adjustment

Raises:

ValueError – width is not positive.

set_data(bardata: Sequence[Sequence[float | int]], top: float, hlines: Sequence[float | int] | None = None) → None¶

Store bar data, bargraph top and horizontal line positions.

Parameters:

  • bardata – a list of bar values.

  • top – maximum value for segments within bardata

  • hlines – None or a bar value marking horizontal line positions

bar values are [ segment1, segment2, … ] lists where top is the maximal value corresponding to the top of the bar graph and segment1, segment2, … are the values for the top of each segment of this bar. Simple bar graphs will only have one segment in each bar value.

Eg: if top is 100 and there is a bar value of [ 80, 30 ] then the top of this bar will be at 80% of full height of the graph and it will have a second segment that starts at 30%.

set_segment_attributes(attlist: Sequence[str | tuple[str, str]], hatt: list[str] | None = None, satt: Mapping[tuple[int, int], str] | None = None) → None¶

Set the display attributes to use for the bar graph’s segments.

Parameters:

  • attlist – list containing display attribute or (display attribute, character) tuple for background, first segment, and optionally following segments. ie. len(attlist) == num segments+1 character defaults to ‘ ‘ if not specified.

  • hatt – list containing attributes for horizontal lines. First element is for lines on background, second is for lines on first segment, third is for lines on second segment etc.

  • satt – dictionary containing attributes for smoothed transitions of bars in UTF-8 display mode. The values are in the form:

Raises:

BarGraphError –

attlist has fewer than two entries, or satt is not a mapping of valid (fg, bg) index pairs with fg above bg.

(fg,bg) : attr

fg and bg are integers where 0 is the graph background, 1 is the first segment, 2 is the second, … fg > bg in all values. attr is an attribute with a foreground corresponding to fg and a background corresponding to bg.

If satt is not None and the bar graph is being displayed in a terminal using the UTF-8 encoding then the character cell that is shared between the segments specified will be smoothed with using the UTF-8 vertical eighth characters.

eg: set_segment_attributes( [‘no’, (‘unsure’,”?”), ‘yes’] ) will use the attribute ‘no’ for the background (the area from the top of the graph to the top of the bar), question marks with the attribute ‘unsure’ will be used for the topmost segment of the bar, and the attribute ‘yes’ will be used for the bottom segment of the bar.

smooth_display(disp: list[tuple[int, list[tuple[int, int]]]]) → list[tuple[int, list[tuple[int | tuple[int, int] | tuple[int, int, int], int]]]]¶

Smooth (col, row*8) display into (col, row) display using UTF vertical eighth characters.

The characters are represented as bar_type tuple values (fg, bg, 1-7) where fg is the lower segment, bg is the upper segment and 1-7 is the vertical eighth character to use.

Raises:

BarGraphError – the smoothed rows do not add up to the graph height.

use_smoothed() → bool¶

Return whether smoothed (sub-character resolution) rendering can be used.

ProgressBar¶

class urwid.ProgressBar(normal: Hashable, complete: Hashable, current: float = 0, done: int = 100, satt: Hashable = None)¶

Flow widget that displays a completion percentage as a bar of Unicode block characters.

Build the progress bar with the given display attributes and range.

Parameters:

  • normal – display attribute for incomplete part of progress bar

  • complete – display attribute for complete part of progress bar

  • current – current progress

  • done – progress amount at 100%

  • satt – display attribute for smoothed part of bar where the foreground of satt corresponds to the normal part and the background corresponds to the complete part. Smoothing requires UTF-8 encoding. If satt is None then no smoothing will be done.

>>> from urwid import LineBox
>>> pb = ProgressBar("a", "b")
>>> pb
<ProgressBar flow widget>
>>> print(pb.get_text())
0 %
>>> pb.set_completion(34.42)
>>> print(pb.get_text())
34 %
>>> class CustomProgressBar(ProgressBar):
...     def get_text(self):
...         return "Foobar"
>>> cpb = CustomProgressBar("a", "b")
>>> print(cpb.get_text())
Foobar
>>> for x in range(101):
...     cpb.set_completion(x)
...     s = cpb.render((10,))
>>> cpb2 = CustomProgressBar("a", "b", satt="c")
>>> for x in range(101):
...     cpb2.set_completion(x)
...     s = cpb2.render((10,))
>>> pb = ProgressBar("a", "b", satt="c")
>>> pb.set_completion(34.56)
>>> print(LineBox(pb).render((20,)))
┌──────────────────┐
│      ▏34 %       │
└──────────────────┘

Terminal¶

class urwid.Terminal(command: tuple[str | bytes | os.PathLike[str] | os.PathLike[bytes], ...] | list[str | bytes | os.PathLike[str] | os.PathLike[bytes]] | Callable[[], Any] | None, env: Mapping[str, str] | Iterable[tuple[str, str]] | None = None, main_loop: event_loop.EventLoop | None = None, escape_sequence: str | None = None, encoding: str = 'utf-8')¶

Widget that runs a child process (or callable) and renders its terminal output.

Initialize a terminal emulator widget.

command is the command to execute inside the terminal, provided as a list of the command followed by its arguments. If ‘command’ is None, the command is the current user’s shell. You can also provide a callable instead of a command, which will be executed in the subprocess.

env can be used to pass custom environment variables. If omitted, os.environ is used.

main_loop should be provided, because the canvas state machine needs to act on input from the PTY master device. This object must have watch_file and remove_watch_file methods.

escape_sequence is the urwid key symbol which should be used to break out of the terminal widget. If it’s not specified, ctrl a is used.

encoding specifies the encoding that is being used when local keypresses in Unicode are encoded into raw bytes. UTF-8 is used by default. Set this to the encoding of your terminal if you need to transmit characters to the spawned process in non-UTF8 encoding. Applies to Python 3.x only.

Note

If you notice your Terminal instance is not printing unicode glyphs correctly, make sure the global encoding for urwid is set to utf8 with urwid.set_encoding("utf8"). See Encodings Supported for more details.

add_watch() → None¶

Register the pty with the main loop, when there is one, so feed() runs on new child output.

beep() → None¶

Emit a “beep” signal for anything listening on this widget.

change_focus(has_focus: bool) → None¶

Ignore SIGINT if this widget has focus.

feed() → None¶

Read pending output from the pty and feed it to the terminal, terminating the child on EOF.

flush_responses() → None¶

Write every buffered response to the pty and clear the buffer.

get_cursor_coords(size: tuple[int, int]) → tuple[int, int] | None¶

Return the cursor coordinates for this terminal.

keypress(size: tuple[int, int], key: str) → str | None¶

Translate key into the byte sequence the child process expects and write it to the pty.

Returns:

None when the widget used key, or key when it did not: the child has exited, the key is handed down to the parent outside a key grab, or the linux terminal type the child is given has no byte form for it, as for a cursor or function key with shift, meta or ctrl.

leds(which: Literal['clear', 'scroll_lock', 'num_lock', 'caps_lock']) → None¶

Emit a “leds” signal asking the display to set keyboard LED state which.

mouse_event(size: tuple[int, int], event: str, button: int, col: int, row: int, focus: bool) → bool | None¶

Report a mouse event to the child in the tracking mode and the encoding the child turned on.

The report bytes are the ones xterm sends for the same event.

Returns:

True when the child tracks the mouse, also for an event its tracking mode does not report. Such events are a drag under mode 1000, the release of a wheel button, and under X10 compatibility mode (9) anything but a press of buttons 1 to 3. False when the event is left to the parent, in these cases:

  • the child has exited;

  • the child does not track the mouse, or tracks it in highlight mode (1001), which is not implemented;

  • the view is scrolled back from the screen the child sees;

  • the event is not a press, a release or a drag.

remove_watch() → None¶

Unregister the pty from the main loop, when there is one.

render(size: tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → TermCanvas¶

Resize the terminal to size, read any pending child output, and return the terminal canvas.

respond(string: str) → None¶

Respond to the underlying application with ‘string’.

set_termsize(width: int, height: int) → None¶

Tell the pty the terminal window is now width by height characters.

set_title(title: str) → None¶

Emit a “title” signal with the terminal’s new title.

spawn() → None¶

Fork the child process running command and connect it to a new pty.

terminate() → None¶

Stop watching the pty, end the child process and close the pty master.

Signals escalate from SIGHUP to SIGKILL until the child exits. A child that may not be signalled, such as a setuid program, only gets the hangup from closing the master. It is then waited for at most one second, and left unreaped if it keeps running.

touch_term(width: int, height: int) → None¶

Spawn the child process if needed, then resize the pty and terminal canvas to width by height.

wait_and_feed(timeout: float = 1.0) → None¶

Block up to timeout seconds for pty output, then read and process whatever has arrived.

Scroll Widget Classes¶

Scrollable¶

class urwid.Scrollable(widget: WrappedScrollWidget, force_forward_keypress: bool = False, *, delegate_selectable: bool = False)¶

Box widget decoration that makes a fixed or flow widget vertically scrollable.

Box widget that makes a fixed or flow widget vertically scrollable.

Note

Focusable widgets are handled, including switching focus, but possibly not intuitively, depending on the arrangement of widgets.

When switching focus to a widget that is ouside of the visible part of the original widget, the canvas scrolls up/down to the focused widget.

It would be better to scroll until the next focusable widget is in sight first. But for that to work we must somehow obtain a list of focusable rows in the original canvas.

Parameters:

  • widget – fixed or flow widget to scroll.

  • force_forward_keypress – pass every key to widget first, even when it shows no cursor.

  • delegate_selectable – take the input focus only when widget is selectable. A widget that is not, such as a Text, then cannot be scrolled by keys.

Raises:

ValueError – widget is neither a FIXED nor a FLOW widget.

get_scrollpos(size: tuple[int, int] | None = None, focus: bool = False) → int¶

Return the current scrolling position.

Lower limit is 0, upper limit is the maximum number of rows with the given maxcol minus maxrow.

..note::

The returned value may be too low or too high if the position has changed but the widget wasn’t rendered yet.

keypress(size: tuple[int, int], key: str) → str | None¶

Handle scrolling keys, forwarding everything else to the wrapped widget when appropriate.

mouse_event(size: tuple[int, int], event: str, button: int, col: int, row: int, focus: bool) → bool | None¶

Forward a mouse event to the wrapped widget, adjusting the row for the current scroll position.

render(size: tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → CompositeCanvas¶

Render the wrapped widget, trimmed to the current scroll position.

rows_max(size: tuple[int, int] | None = None, focus: bool = False) → int¶

Return the number of rows for size.

If size is not given, the currently rendered number of rows is returned.

Raises:

ScrollableError – the wrapped widget is neither a FLOW nor a FIXED widget.

selectable() → bool¶

Return whether the widget accepts the input focus.

Always True, unless delegate_selectable is set: then what the wrapped widget returns.

set_scrollpos(position: SupportsInt) → None¶

Set scrolling position.

If position is positive it is interpreted as lines from the top. If position is negative it is interpreted as lines from the bottom.

Values that are too high or too low values are automatically adjusted during rendering.

sizing() → frozenset[Sizing]¶

Return that this widget is always a box widget.

ScrollBar¶

class urwid.ScrollBar(widget: WrappedScrollableWidget, thumb_char: str = ScrollbarSymbols.FULL_BLOCK, trough_char: str = ' ', side: Literal['left', 'right'] = 'right', width: int = 1, *, visible: bool | None = None, scroll_by_focus: bool = False, delegate_selectable: bool = False, end_markers: tuple[str, str] | None = None, attr: Hashable = None, focus_attr: Hashable = None, thumb_attr: Hashable = None, thumb_focus_attr: Hashable = None, marker_dim_attr: Hashable = None)¶

Box widget decoration that adds a scrollbar alongside a scrollable wrapped widget.

Box widget that adds a scrollbar to widget.

Parameters:

  • widget –

    box widget that has, or wraps a widget that has, the following methods:

    • get_scrollpos takes the arguments size and focus and returns the index of the first visible row.

    • set_scrollpos (optional; needed for mouse click and drag support on the scrollbar) takes the index of the first visible row.

    • rows_max takes size and focus and returns the total number of rows widget can render.

  • thumb_char – character used for the scrollbar handle.

  • trough_char – character used for the space above and below the handle.

  • side – side the scrollbar is drawn on, 'left' or 'right'.

  • width – number of columns the scrollbar uses, at least 1.

  • visible – when the scrollbar is drawn: None draws it only when widget needs scrolling, True always, so the wrapped widget always gets the same width, and False never, so the wrapped widget gets the full width and is still scrolled by keys and wheel.

  • scroll_by_focus – let a click or drag on the scrollbar scroll a ListBox, which has no set_scrollpos, by moving its focus to the widget at the top of the new view. The focus then changes without passing through the ListBox keypress or mouse_event, so this is off by default for code that tracks the focus there.

  • delegate_selectable – take the input focus only when widget is selectable; a ListBox created with focus_when_empty=False is not while it is empty. Off by default, so a wrapped widget that is not selectable can still be scrolled by keys.

  • end_markers – characters drawn in the first and the last scrollbar row, or None for no markers, such as (ScrollBar.Symbols.ARROW_TRIANGLE_UP, ScrollBar.Symbols.ARROW_TRIANGLE_DOWN). They are drawn only when the scrollbar has at least 3 rows, and a click on one scrolls one step towards its end, as the mouse wheel does.

  • attr – display attribute of the trough and the end markers.

  • focus_attr – display attribute of the trough and the end markers when rendered in focus; None uses attr.

  • thumb_attr – display attribute of the thumb; None uses attr.

  • thumb_focus_attr – display attribute of the thumb when rendered in focus; None uses thumb_attr when it is set, and focus_attr otherwise.

  • marker_dim_attr – display attribute of an end marker whose end of the content is visible; None draws it like the other marker. An end counts as visible only when the first or last row of the content is on screen. A custom widget scrolled by items rather than rows, through SupportsRelativeScroll, cannot report cut-off rows, so for it an end counts once its first or last item is on screen.

Raises:

  • ValueError – widget is not a BOX widget, or end_markers is not a pair.

  • TypeError – widget does not wrap anything that supports the scrolling protocol.

Symbols¶

alias of ScrollbarSymbols

keypress(size: tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], key: str) → str | None¶

Forward a keypress to the wrapped widget, at the size it is rendered at within size.

mouse_event(size: tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], event: str, button: int, col: int, row: int, focus: bool) → bool | None¶

Handle a mouse event, dispatching it to the scrollbar thumb/trough or to the wrapped widget.

A press of button 1 on the scrollbar, and the drag that follows it, move the thumb top to the pointer row. So does its release on displays that report the button of a release, such as curses, which send no drags. A press of button 1 on an end marker scrolls one step towards that end, as the mouse wheel does, and the drag and release that follow it do nothing. Events in the wrapped widget’s columns go to it. On the scrollbar, the vertical mouse wheel of a widget without set_scrollpos (such as ListBox) is passed on, together with the drags and releases described below; other events there are not.

A drag or release goes where its press went: a drag started on the scrollbar keeps moving the thumb over the wrapped widget’s columns, and a drag started on the wrapped widget stays with it over the scrollbar. A drag or release whose press was not seen here, such as the end of a drag and drop started in another widget, goes to the wrapped widget. Events outside this widget never reach it, so a release there is not seen; the next press here starts over.

render(size: tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → Canvas¶

Render the wrapped widget together with the scrollbar, when scrolling is needed.

A flow size renders the wrapped widget at its flow rows, so it never needs scrolling.

rows(size: tuple[int], focus: bool = False) → int¶

Return the rows of the wrapped widget at the width it is rendered at.

With visible True the scrollbar always takes its columns, so the wrapped widget gets the rest.

Raises:

AttributeError – the wrapped widget has no rows(), as a Scrollable has none.

property scroll_by_focus: bool¶

Whether a click or drag on the scrollbar scrolls a ListBox by moving its focus.

property scrollbar_side: Literal['left', 'right']¶

Where to display the scrollbar; must be ‘left’ or ‘right’.

property scrollbar_width: int¶

Columns the scrollbar uses.

property scrolling_base_widget: SupportsScroll¶

Nearest original_widget that is compatible with the scrolling API.

Raises:

ScrollableError – no wrapped widget supports the scrolling protocol.

selectable() → bool¶

Return whether the widget accepts the input focus.

Always True, unless delegate_selectable is set: then what the wrapped widget returns.

sizing() → frozenset[Sizing]¶

Return that this widget is always a box widget.

property visible: bool | None¶

When the scrollbar is drawn: None when scrolling is needed, True always, False never.

class urwid.widget.scrollable.ScrollbarSymbols(*values)¶

Common symbols suitable for scrollbar.

The thumb and trough symbols come first, and the ARROW_* pairs for the end markers follow them.

Only these members are also drawn on terminals without UTF-8, where the others are drawn as ?:

  • ASCII: ARROW_ASCII_UP and ARROW_ASCII_DOWN.

  • DEC special graphics: MEDIUM_SHADE, DRAWING_LIGHT, BLACK_VERTICAL_RECTANGLE and MIDDLE_DOT.

ARROW_ASCII_UP = '^'¶
ARROW_DOWN = '↓'¶
